ADTNM Comprehensive Study Guide

Status: Active Research Framework (Work in Progress) · License: MIT (LICENSE) · Standards Alignment: IETF RFC 9675 & IRTF RFC 7575-Inspired · Simulator: The ONE (Java, JDK 17+)

ADTNM (Autonomic Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Network Management) is an architectural framework for autonomic management of delay/disruption-tolerant networks (DTNs). Inspired by IETF RFC 9675 (Delay-Tolerant Networking Management Architecture, Birrane et al., November 2024) and IRTF RFC 7575 (Autonomic Networking, Behringer et al., June 2015), ADTNM decouples network management from packet forwarding. Established DTN protocols (SprayAndWait, ProphetV2, MaxProp, Epidemic, and DtnmaRouter) operate unchanged as managed substrates, while lightweight adapters connect them to a unified local DtnmaAgent controller running standardized Externally Defined Data (EDD) telemetry, declarative state-based rules (SRL), and deterministic safety shields (S1–S4). An optional constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) reinforcement learning (RL) module (M3, ShieldedCmdpRlAgent) is marked Implemented, experimental and did not outperform hand-written declarative rules (M2) in v1.0 evaluations.

Chapter 1: Executive Summary

Scope: Active Research Framework (MIT License) · Frozen Confirmatory Evaluation: v1.0-freeze (n = 11 seeds, 627 urban VDTN runs) · Exploratory Follow-Up: v1.0-exp-controls (176 runs) · Target: Standalone <= 2 PDF pages

1. Architectural Identity & Core Thesis

ADTNM (Autonomic Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Network Management) is an architectural management framework for challenged vehicular and mobile wireless networks implemented in Java atop The ONE simulator. Drawing inspiration from IETF RFC 9675 (DTN Management Architecture, Nov 2024) and IRTF RFC 7575 (Autonomic Networking, June 2015), ADTNM decouples network management semantics from bundle forwarding heuristics:

  • Existing DTN protocols (EpidemicRouter, ProphetV2Router, MaxPropRouter, SprayAndWaitRouter, DtnmaRouter) remain managed substrates whose underlying path estimators stay untouched.
  • A uniform DtnmaAgent engine wraps any substrate through a thin adapter (Managed*Router, averaging 253.5 non-comment lines of Java) to execute 11 Externally Defined Data (EDD) telemetry sensors, declarative State-Based Rules (SRL), discrete P0–P7 Control Profiles, a deterministic Safety Shield (S1–S4), and atomic Application Resource Identifier (ARI) audit logging (100.00% replayable offline).
  • An optional Constrained MDP (CMDP) reinforcement learning (RL) planner (M3, ShieldedCmdpRlAgent) is included strictly as an Implemented, experimental module. In v1.0 evaluations it trailed hand-written SRL rules (M2).

All metrics trace programmatically to provenance_ledger.json. Confirmatory runs (7103–7207) and post-freeze exploratory controls (7211–7307) never share statistical pools.

B. Honest Negatives & Post-Freeze Exploratory Controls (176 Runs, Unadjusted p_unadj)

WARNING

Essential Caveats for Academic Review 1. Failed Survival Non-Inferiority (H2_orig): Pre-registered survival non-inferiority (M2 within -5 pp of M1-U in stress) failed: M2 trailed M1-U by -5.48 ± 1.96 pp (83.8 vs 90.7/126, 0/11 wins, p_unadj = 9.65e-5). 2. Experimental M3 RL Module Loses to M2: Across stress (bulk 63% vs 66%, alive 76.0 vs 83.8) and benign (80% vs 82%) runs, linear Q-learning underperformed SRL (M2), underscoring why RL remains optional. 3. Exploratory Causal Attribution (v1.0-exp-controls): Static M0e-25 (SoC < 0.25) matched M2 end survival (83.8 vs 83.8/126, p = 1.0), whereas M2-LocalOnly dropped to 80.0/126 — isolating how much survival derived from M2's 0.25 guard wave. Meanwhile, single-copy group flooding (M1-F-Group) slashed flood energy from 118.7 kJ (M1-F) to 201.6 J (99.5/126 survivors), though median adoption (482.9 s) still missed the 300 s Event A burst and trailed M2 in Benign bulk (76.0% vs 82.0%).

3. Five Open Research & Engineering Decisions (v1.1 Roadmap)

  1. Local Energy-Drain Hysteresis vs. Benign Throughput: Incorporate continuous EDD_ENERGY_DRAIN slope awareness into rules_vdtn.txt so local autonomy matches or exceeds M1-U stress survival without needing a 0.25 remote guard wave (>= 90 survivors while holding ~82% benign bulk).
  2. Scope of the M3 RL Module: Retain M3 purely as an experimental negative control in v1.0 manuscripts, or explore low-dimensional hazard-feature contextual bandits for v1.1.
  3. Closed-Loop Remote Manager Synthesis: Replace scenario-scheduled Manager waves (M1-U, M1-F-Group) with adaptive policy synthesis computed dynamically from delayed AoI/uplink telemetry.
  4. Report Accounting & CI Hygiene: Separate ACK-pruned duplicate evictions from live drops inside DtnmaDecisionReport (53 benign prunes counted as drops in 1 h smoke while unique_critical_lost = 0) and modernize .github/workflows/ci.yml onto headless smoke + replay checks.
  5. Domain Expansion & Schema Cleanup: Empirically validate scenarios/rules_uav.txt with explicit priority-10 recovery fallback and retire unused legacy primal-dual configuration keys (lambda = 0.0).

Chapter 2: Zero-Background Primer for Newcomers

Target Audience: New team members and reviewers with zero prior DTN, IETF RFC, or simulator background.
Prerequisites: None. Acronyms expanded in full on first appearance.

1. What Makes a DTN Different from the Internet?

On the everyday Internet (TCP/IP), you assume two things are true almost all the time: 1. An end-to-end path exists between your phone and a server right now. 2. Round-trip delays are tens of milliseconds, so asking "Did you get that packet?" happens nearly instantaneously.

In a Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Network (DTN) — disaster-response vehicular fleets, challenged urban transit, or unmanned aerial relays (vDTN, UAV) — both assumptions break: - Nodes move out of radio range or behind urban obstacles, run on batteries, or lose radios for minutes to hours. - There may never be a simultaneous path from sender A to receiver D: A hands data to B at t = 5 min, B drives across town, meets C at t = 22 min, and C delivers to D at t = 40 min.

Because packets cannot simply wait on a wire, DTNs use Store-Carry-Forward (RFC 9171, Bundle Protocol Version 7, Burleigh et al., Jan 2022). Data units called bundles sit inside node flash/RAM buffers while carriers physically move through space.

TIP

INTUITION Think of DTN bundles like relay baton messages carried by couriers. If a courier runs out of backpack space (buffer overflow), critical triage dispatches (CRIT_) risk being thrown in the ditch to make room for low-priority telemetry logs (BULK_), OR a courier sprints back and forth handing copies to everyone until their battery dies (energy blackout).

2. Four Classical Routing Strategies — And Why Routing Alone Isn't Management

Before ADTNM, researchers invented different forwarding algorithms deciding who gets a copy of a bundle during brief wireless encounters (contacts):

Router Class Forwarding Idea Strength Failure Mode Under Stress
Epidemic (EpidemicRouter) Flood every missing bundle to every neighbor met Minimal latency when buffers & batteries are infinite Rapidly exhausts buffers and batteries (14–16/126 survivors in energy blackouts)
PRoPHETv2 (ProphetV2Router, RFC 6693) Track encounter probabilities P(a, b); forward only to higher-probability carriers Avoids blind flooding in structured mobility Drops low-utility critical packets when congestion hits, still drains batteries
MaxProp (MaxPropRouter) Estimate path delivery likelihood via Dijkstra over encounter rates + ACK deletion High throughput under moderate load Drops bundles by internal hop/cost order rather than operational criticality
Spray-and-Wait (SprayAndWaitRouter) Binary mode: hand half of L remaining copy tokens (L_init = 6) per contact until L = 1 (direct delivery only) Bounded replication overhead (<= L copies) Rigid static L under surges unless dynamically throttled or prioritized

Notice the key distinction: routing algorithms answer "who should carry this next?" — management answers "given scarce battery, surging traffic, and critical-safety goals right now, how much bulk replication, ingress admission, and buffer space should the node permit?"

3. Why Centralized Management Fails in DTNs (RFC 9675 & RFC 7575)

In an ordinary cloud cluster (SNMP / RESTCONF), a central Manager continuously polls switches every few seconds and pushes fixes immediately. In a DTN, trying to manage nodes solely from a central ground station hits a physics wall:

  1. Timescale Mismatch (Stale Control Loops): When a remote Manager sits behind opportunistic relays, its control bundle takes hundreds to thousands of seconds to reach agents (e.g., T50 = 483 s even with group-flooded dissemination in exploratory controls, or T90 = 3336 s with unicast in confirmatory stress). By the time a "slow down!" command arrives for a 300 s traffic surge (Event A), the surge is over — causing stale throttling during calm traffic.
  2. Control Storm Overhead: Flooding individual unicast control updates across a dense wireless DTN consumes massive radio energy (118.7 kJ in M1-F vs 2.58 kJ in M2), killing nodes via management traffic itself.

Two IETF/IRTF specifications define the conceptual solution ADTNM adapts: - IETF RFC 9675 (Delay-Tolerant Networking Management Architecture, Birrane et al., Nov 2024): Replaces synchronous polling with asynchronous Agents executing local State-Based Rules (SRL) parameterized by locally observable Externally Defined Data (EDD), emitting compact Application Resource Identifier (ARI) audit records and executing Controls autonomously when disconnected from a Manager. - IRTF RFC 7575 (Autonomic Networking, Behringer et al., June 2015): Defines autonomic self-management (self-configuring, self-healing, self-optimizing, self-protecting) alongside explicit safety/human constraints — autonomy operates strictly inside hard guardrails rather than unrestrained black-box optimization.

NOTE

SUPERVISOR NOTE ADTNM is RFC 9675-inspired and RFC 7575-inspired. It borrows their architectural separation of roles, data models, and closed-loop constraints inside Java objects; it does not claim byte-level CBOR wire compatibility with IETF DTNMA drafts or ION. See Appendix A.

4. How The ONE Simulator Runs a Scenario

The ONE (Opportunistic Network Environment, n:\R&D\cog\the-one\) advances simulated wall time in discrete 0.1 s steps (tick interval, MovementModel.worldSize & Scenario.updateInterval = 0.1):

  1. Scenario Parsing: .txt config files (scenarios/scenario_dtnma.txt layered atop dtnma_params_default.txt) instantiate groups of DTNHost nodes, movement models (e.g., Helsinki MapBasedMovement), radio interfaces, EnergyModel batteries, traffic generators (CRIT_ and BULK_ prefixes), and one MessageRouter prototype per group.
  2. Every 0.1 s Simulation Tick: - Nodes advance along roads/trajectories; radios discover neighbors within range and open/close Connection objects. - Active transfers advance byte-by-byte at transmitSpeed; completed transfers fire MessageListener hooks and energy consumption debits (scanEnergy, transmitEnergy, receiveEnergy). - Each node's router executes update() (DtnmaRouter.update() delegates to DtnmaAgent.update(...)), which runs fast per-tick protection + 30 s-interval autonomic decision epochs.
  3. End-of-Simulation Reporting: Registered Report classes flush raw .txt files into the scenario's reports/ folder (MessageStatsReport, DtnmaRlMetricsReport, DtnmaAuditReport, DtnmaRecoveryTimelineReport).

5. Five Real Failure Modes That Motivated ADTNM

Every mechanism in Chapters 04a–04d traces directly to five failure behaviors observed directly in simulator experiments:

  1. Silent Critical Drop Under Congestion: Without explicit priority classification and reserve enforcement, critical CRIT_ fault alerts are dropped FIFO/cost-wise alongside bulk traffic (Epidemic loses 100% of unique critical messages in vDTN Overload).
  2. Stale Redundant Replicas Starving Live Traffic: Once a critical bundle reaches its destination, redundant copies still in relay buffers keep displacing fresh un-ACKed payloads until explicit delivery acknowledgments (ACKs) prune them.
  3. Battery Blackout Collapse: Aggressive routers (Epidemic, MaxProp) transmit bulk relays until SoC -> 0, knocking out 87%–89% of the fleet (14–16/126 survivors) and severing connectivity for future critical dispatches.
  4. Delayed Remote Stale-Throttling: Unicast/flooded Manager rules (M1-U, M1-F) suffer delayed delivery, throttling nodes after short surges recover and crippling benign/post-event throughput (389.1 stale throttle node-s/N in Event A).
  5. Unsafe Exploration & Voluntary Hold Bugs: Early unshielded RL policies (M3 predecessors) explored aggressive HIGH_SPRAY_OPEN during dense storms (41% critical occupancy buildup) or stalled on P0 when mis-rewarded — fixed via hard shield S1–S4 and reward recalibration (M3 still remains optional and secondary to M2).

Chapter 3: Architecture Overview

Documented Commit: d4a159f | Core Principle: Routers are managed substrates governed by an RFC 9675/7575-inspired autonomic management layer.

1. Four-Plane Architectural Stack

ADTNM decomposes DTN operations into four decoupled planes inside src/routing/ and src/report/:

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. OBSERVABILITY & PROVENANCE PLANE                                         |
|    DtnmaAuditReport (16-col ARI trace) · DtnmaRlMetricsReport (Cohorts/CDF) |
|    DtnmaDecisionReport · DtnmaRecoveryTimelineReport · offline Replay Tool  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                      ^  Records every EDD, rule, shield, ARI
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. AUTONOMIC DECISION & POLICY PLANE (DtnmaAgent)                           |
|    SRL Rule Parser (12-line vDTN ruleset) · Optional M3 RL (experimental)    |
|    DtnmaSafetyShield (S1..S4 + Liveness) -> Active Control Profile (P0..P7) |
|    Remote Overlay Slot (upserts Manager DOWNLINK/GROUP rule, TTL/priority)   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
        ^  11 EDDs (dt = 30 s)                        v  Actuates L, bp, ing
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. SUBSTRATE ADAPTATION PLANE (DtnmaManagedRouter + Managed*Router)         |
|    Thin adapters (~253.5 mean non-comment LOC) for SnW, PRoPHETv2, MaxProp, |
|    Epidemic; shared 5-tier Queue + ACK-first eviction + ByteBudget Guard     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                      ^  Native routing heuristics
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. FORWARDING & PHYSICAL SUBSTRATE PLANE (The ONE Engine + Routers)         |
|    DTNHost · EnergyModel · MovementModel · ActiveRouter · SprayAndWait,     |
|    ProphetV2, MaxProp, Epidemic, DtnmaRouter                                |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Why This Layering Matters

  • Strict Separation of Concerns: Changing a mobility model (Layer 1) or swapping SprayAndWait for MaxProp (Layer 2) does not alter DtnmaAgent rules (Layer 3) or audit logs (Layer 4).
  • Router-Agnostic Portability: A single declarative rule file (scenarios/rules_vdtn.txt, 12 lines) governs four mathematically distinct forwarding algorithms without rewriting per-router Java scheduling logic.

2. Three Coupled Timescales of Control

ADTNM operates simultaneously across three distinct temporal scales (implemented+tested):

Timescale Cadence Trigger / Actors Responsibilities
Fast Reactive Protection Per tick (0.1 s) & per packet checkReceiving, tryAllMessages, DtnmaRouter queue/eviction Reject un-ACKed BULK_ when byte reservation full (maxOvershoot = 1); evict ACKed criticals first, then BULK_; respect active ingressMode (0/1/2) and hard energy floors; prune delivered copies via peer contact ACK IDs (4 B/ID)
Local Autonomic Control Every dt = 30.0 s (dtnmaTelemetryIntervalSec) EddTelemetrySampler -> DtnmaAgent -> SRL / (M3) -> DtnmaSafetyShield Compute 11 local + neighbor EDDs from 16 B contact beacons; evaluate priority-latched SRL rules (or optional M3 RL Q-critic); filter P0..P7 through hard constraints S1–S4; emit atomic snapshot + ARI://... audit row
Remote Manager Overlay Minutes to hours (DTN propagation) Ground/Manager host -> Uplink telemetry (648 B gossip / status) & Downlink CTRL_ bundles (M1-U, M1-F, M1-F-Group, M2) Inject or refresh time-bounded remote overlay rules via applyDownlinkControlBundle() (e.g., pre-configuring shieldEnergyMin = 0.25); logs adoption CDFs (T10..T95) and Age of Information (AoI)

IMPORTANT

FORMAL / CODE Because DTN propagation delays exceed surge durations (300 s Event A vs 483 s–3336 s remote median/T90 adoption), the Local Autonomic loop (30 s) handles transient spikes (VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE), while the Remote Overlay provides slower strategic configuration updates (dtnmaControlPriority = 100 when active). See DtnmaAgent.java:634-733 and 1200-1323.

Mechanism 01: Agent–Manager Architectural Split & Multi-Timescale Overlay

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Decouples node-local operational survival (DtnmaAgent) from supervisory campaign orchestration (Manager host), resolving the control-loop delay wall in Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Networks (DTNs) where Manager round trips span hundreds to thousands of seconds (483 s–3336 s).

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Pure centralized polling (SNMP style): Rejected; Manager commands arrive stale after transient 300 s surges terminate (389.1 stale throttle node-s/N in M1-U).
  • Pure isolated agents (M2-LocalOnly): Avoids control traffic (0 J), yet misses global mission threshold updates when local heuristics remain static (80.0/126 stress survival vs 83.8/126 in M2).
  • Selected hybrid split (RFC 9675-inspired): Fast local SRL (30 s) handles immediate bursts; delayed Manager downlinks (priority >= 100) inject or refresh time-bounded configuration overlays.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Manager hosts inject CTRL_UPDATE_ / CTRL_GROUP_ bundles -> Carried opportunistically over The ONE contacts -> Intercepted cleanly in DtnmaAgent.checkReceiving / applyDownlinkControlBundle (DtnmaAgent.java:1200-1323) -> Upserted into the local StateBasedRule table (overlay slot) and evaluated alongside static rules during the 30 s DtnmaAgent.update tick.

4. Inputs & Configuration

dtnmaConfig flags in DtnmaConfig.java: isAutonomicMode (Master toggle), isAutonomicRlMode, dtnmaRemoteControlOnly, dtnmaControlPriority (100 for active overlay vs <0 disabled), dtnmaControlTimeoutSec, dtnmaTelemetryIntervalSec (30.0 s).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

  • Effective rule priority Peff(r) = Poverlay(r) when active downlink overlay has not expired (now <= expireTime), superseding static rules at priority <= 99.
  • Control Age of Information: AoI(t) = t - tlast_uplink_rx, logged per 10.0 s sample window (AOI_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SEC).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:634-733 (evaluateAutonomyEngine), :1200-1323 (applyDownlinkControlBundle, upsertDownlinkOverlayRule)
  • src/routing/DtnmaConfig.java:1-90

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

DtnmaAuditReport active_ari traces remote overlays; DtnmaRlMetricsReport records downlink_t90_sec, aoi_mean_sec, aoi_p95_sec, aoi_peak_sec, and # WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Downlink bundles expire automatically if t > t_rx + ttlSec; corrupt payloads missing valid rule syntax are ignored cleanly without clearing static local SRL safety rules.

9. Worked Mini-Example

In confirmatory compB_multitimescale (seed 7103), Manager wave W1 starts at t = 3601 s. In M1-U, 90% adoption takes 3336.2 s mean across seeds (T90), so Event A's 300 s burst already ended before throttling engages — whereas M2 reacts locally at 3360.5 s via VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE.

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze). Earlier prototypes lacked per-wave CDF adoption logging (# WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF added prior to freeze).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Directly operationalizes RFC 9675 Sec 3 (asynchronous autonomy). Limitation: Manager campaigns in v1.0 are schedule-driven rather than dynamically synthesized from uplink telemetry.

Mechanism 02: Externally Defined Data (EDD) Telemetry Sampler (11 Indicators)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Provides a uniform, router-independent 11-element numerical state vector sampled every 30.0 s, preventing heterogeneous routers from inventing incompatible internal congestion signals.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Router-private counters: Breaks portability; every rule file would require router-specific Java bindings.
  • Raw instantaneous queue readings: Noisy under rapid bundle arrivals/departures, causing profile chatter.
  • Selected EWMA + sliding-window EDD sampler: Smooths short bursts while keeping deterministic state vectors across routers.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Every 30 s -> EddTelemetrySampler.sampleAndCompute(host, managedRouter, now) queries getBufferOccupancyRatio(), getCriticalOccupancyRatio(), getEnergySoc(), getConnections(), host speed from coordinates, and neighbor 16 B beacons -> stores double[11] indexed by EDD_* constants.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Configured via dtnmaTelemetryIntervalSec (30.0 s). Hard-coded constants (EddTelemetrySampler.java:26-44): ALPHA_DRIFT = 0.30, ALPHA_SPEED = 0.25, DENSITY_WINDOW_SEC = 300.0, P_INIT = 0.75, DEFAULT_BETA = 0.25, DEFAULT_GAMMA = 0.98, SECONDS_IN_TIME_UNIT = 30.0.

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

  • EDD_QUEUE_RATIO (Q ∈ [0,1]) = (Btotal - Bfree) / Btotal
  • EDD_CRIT_QUEUE_RATIO (Q_c ∈ [0,1]) = \summ ∈ CRIT |m| / Btotal
  • EDD_QUEUE_DRIFT: Δ Q_t = αd (Q_t - Qt-1) + (1 - αd)Δ Qt-1, αd = 0.30
  • EDD_NODE_DENSITY: count of distinct peers seen within sliding [now - 300.0 s, now] window
  • EDD_ACTIVE_CONNECTIONS: current open Connection count; EDD_NODE_SPEED: EWMA speed (αs = 0.25)
  • EDD_ENERGY_SOC (E ∈ [0,1]) = clamp(Erem / Einit); EDD_ENERGY_DRAIN: EWMA battery depletion rate (computed and exposed for v1.1 slope triggers, unused in v1.0 rules).
  • EDD_NEIGHBOR_MIN_QUEUE (Qnbr^{min}), EDD_NEIGHBOR_QUEUE_GRAD = Q - Qnbr^{min}, and EDD_DEST_PROB (Pdest ∈ [0,1] encounter table).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/EddTelemetrySampler.java:26-36 (11 EDD_* constants), :140-320 (sampleAndCompute, getEddValue, getMobilityClass)

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

All primary state variables are logged verbatim per decision epoch inside columns 5–11 of DtnmaAuditReport (Q, CritQ, dQ, Dens, Con, SoC, ...).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Empty buffers (B_total <= 0) safely return 0.0. Mobility class (getMobilityClass) maps < 2.2 m/s -> 0 (slow), 2.2–9.5 -> 1 (vehicular), >= 9.5 m/s or interfaces > 1 -> 2 (fast/multi-radio).

9. Worked Mini-Example

At t = 3360.5 s on node 53 (seed 7103), EddTelemetrySampler reports Q = 0.9192, CritQ = 0.0056, dQ = 0.0084, Dens = 15.0, SoC = 0.9228. Notice VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE prints 0.92 and 0.01 rounded in audit explanations while comparing exact double values (0.9192 >= 0.88, 0.00839 >= 0.008).

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (10 EDDs actively used in rules/RL; EDD_ENERGY_DRAIN is Implemented, experimental / unused in v1.0).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Translates RFC 9675 EDD telemetry cleanly across 4 heterogeneous routers.

Mechanism 03: Five-Tier Priority Queue & ACK-First Eviction Order

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Guarantees critical fault bundles (CRIT_) and control bundles (CTRL_) are never displaced by bulk telemetry (BULK_), and already-delivered critical copies are pruned cleanly before risking live un-ACKed payloads.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • FIFO / Random drop: Loses CRIT_ payloads under congestion (Epidemic loses up to 100% critical in vDTN overload).
  • 2-tier Crit vs Bulk without ACK awareness: Keeps dead critical duplicates clogged in RAM, choking subsequent fresh traffic.
  • Selected 5-tier O(N) bucketing:Deterministic, zero allocations per comparison, separates live criticals from ACKed criticals and control frames.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Triggered inside DtnmaAgent.selectNextMessageToRemove(...) (makeRoomForMessage) and reused uniformly across DtnmaRouter and all 4 Managed*Router adapters.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Bundle prefix tags: CRIT_, CTRL_, BULK_; active-sending exclusion flag (excludeMsgBeingSent); deliveredAckSet LRU (512 IDs).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Single-pass scan partitions buffer into 5 buckets, evicting from lowest non-empty tier (using substrate comparator compareByQueueMode within each tier): 1. Tier 0 (Evict First): BULK_ messages 2. Tier 1: Already-ACKed CRIT_ duplicates (deliveredAckSet.contains(id)) 3. Tier 2: Stale/expired/untagged non-critical control frames 4. Tier 3: Active CTRL_ bundles 5. Tier 4 (Evict Last): Un-ACKed live CRIT_ bundles

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaRouter.java:275-291 (5-tier O(N) bucketing), :612-647 (prefix classifiers)
  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:1004-1027 (selectNextMessageToRemove)

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

DtnmaRlMetricsReport distinguishes critical_buffer_dropped (un-ACKed Tier 4) vs critical_buffer_dropped_acked (Tier 1). Reporting Note: DtnmaDecisionReport.java:103-107 aggregates both into Critical Fault Messages Dropped (53 in 1 h smoke vs 0 un-ACKed loss).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Messages currently mid-transfer (isSending) are skipped unless zero other candidates exist. Tested in DtnmaUnitTests (Test1a, Test5, Test7).

9. Worked Mini-Example

In the 1h scenario_dtnma.txt smoke run, 53 CRIT_ copies are dropped from saturated buffers — every single one came from Tier 1 (deliveredAckSet), resulting in unique_critical_lost = 0 (184 delivered out of 262 created across classes).

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze). Replaces earlier Comparator.sort loops (O(N log N) per eviction) with single-pass O(N) bucket scan.

11. Supervisor Rationale

Core contributor to 0 unique critical lost across all 132 managed CompA runs, regardless of forwarding substrate.

Mechanism 04: Byte-Budget Critical Reservation Guard (maxOvershoot)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Stops a buffer full of BULK_ bundles from refusing an incoming CRIT_ or CTRL_ bundle if total buffer size is constrained, OR allowing critical bundles to overrun free-space limits unpredictably.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Strict FIFO admission (DENY_OLDEST): Rejects CRIT_ whenever freeSpace < msgSize and existing CRIT_ cannot make room.
  • Unbounded overshoot: Lets CRIT_ bursts blow past configured node buffer RAM limits.
  • Selected dual incoming byte reservation: Tracks pending/active bytes and enforces an explicit critical byte reserve (maxOvershoot, default 1).

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Executes in evaluateCheckReceiving (DtnmaAgent.java:954-1003 and DtnmaRouter.java:411-474) before makeRoomForMessage.

4. Inputs & Configuration

dtnmaMaxOvershootCount (default 1 byte/packet margin or configurable via DtnmaConfig), node bufferSize, reservedBytes across active incoming transfers.

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Incoming bundle m: - If BULK_: reject with DENIED_NO_SPACE unless evicting only BULK_ + ACKed CRIT_ yields >= |m| bytes (un-ACKed CRIT_ + CTRL_ bytes protected!). - If CRIT_ / CTRL_: permit eviction of lower-priority tiers; clamp total overshoot against bufferSize within maxOvershoot boundary.

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaRouter.java:411-474
  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:954-1003

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

Logs rejections into DtnmaRlMetricsReport (crit_rejected_src, bulk_rejected_src). Zero CRIT_ overshoot violations verified in DtnmaUnitTests.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Test7 & Test8 in DtnmaUnitTests.java explicitly verify 100%-critical full buffer boundary: accepts 0 overshoot past limit while guaranteeing exact capacity reservation.

9. Worked Mini-Example

Node has 5 MB RAM: 4.8 MB is BULK_ and 0.2 MB is CRIT_. A new 300 KB CRIT_ bundle triggers immediate BULK_ eviction; conversely, a new 300 KB BULK_ bundle arriving into 4.9 MB CRIT_ is rejected immediately (DENIED_NO_SPACE).

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Prevents priority inversion at ingress without requiring separate physical queues.

Mechanism 05: Three-Level Ingress Admission Control (INGRESS_)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Slows or stops low-priority BULK_ traffic at the gateway or transit node before congestion propagates downstream and drains peer batteries.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Always accept all bundles: Allows bulk relays to flood stressed neighborhoods until buffers overflow and nodes die (M0b = 54.1/126 alive).
  • Selected 3-mode discrete actuator (ControlAction 0/1/2): Separates external relay intake throttling (Mode 1) from complete local bulk emergency hold (Mode 2).

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Profile P0..P7 sets ingressMode in DtnmaAgent; every new createNewMessage and incoming receiveMessage checks ingressMode before admission.

4. Inputs & Configuration

ControlAction.java:21-38: - 0 = INGRESS_ACCEPT_ALL - 1 = INGRESS_THROTTLE_BULK (reject new transit BULK_ while admitting local critical & control) - 2 = INGRESS_CRITICAL_ONLY (reject all BULK_ creations and transit relays)

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

if (!isCritOrCtrl(m)) {
  if (ingressMode == 2) return DENIED_POLICY;
  if (ingressMode == 1 && isTransitRelay(m)) return DENIED_POLICY;
}

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/ControlAction.java:21-38
  • src/routing/DtnmaPolicyProfile.java:23-32
  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:965-990

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

bulk_rejected_src counters in DtnmaRlMetricsReport; stale_throttle_nodesec tracks node-seconds spent in ingressMode > 0 after an event window ends.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

CRIT_ and CTRL_ bundles bypass ingress locks in every mode (0, 1, 2), preserving emergency reachability even under P0 emergency hold.

9. Worked Mini-Example

Under M0c (static pre-installed throttle guard) in Benign traffic, keeping ingressMode > 0 unnecessarily cuts bulk_delivery_prob to 53.9%; M2 only enters ingressMode = 1 (P1) during surges (VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE) and restores 0 (P4/P2) when queues clear, achieving 82.0% benign bulk (+28.13 pp, H4).

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze). Tier 2 gains on Epidemic (14.5 -> 125.9 alive) come chiefly from Mechanisms 05 + 09 rather than replica caps (Tier 3).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Proves traffic shaping at ingress yields ~100% of the survival benefit without rewriting substrate routing tables.

Mechanism 06: Discrete 8-Tuple Control Profile Catalog (P0–P7)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Compresses continuous, noisy actuator tuning into 8 safety-auditable operating points (P0..P7) shared identically by rule policies (M2), remote overlays (M1), and experimental RL (M3).

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Continuous scalar action space (L, bpRatio separately): Explodes verification complexity and prevents clean bitmask safety masking (8-bit bitmask).
  • Selected 8-profile enum (DtnmaPolicyProfile): Enables 1-byte (11111111) feasibility bitmasking by the safety shield and compact ARI traceability.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

DtnmaRuleParser or ShieldedCmdpRlAgent selects target index a in {0..7} -> DtnmaSafetyShield.enforce(...) applies 8-bit admissibility mask mask[0..7] -> Selected DtnmaPolicyProfile applies (L, backpressureRatio, ingressMode, backpressureEnabled) to adapter setters.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Defined immutably in src/routing/DtnmaPolicyProfile.java:23-32:

ID Profile Name Copy Limit L Backpressure bp Ingress Mode BP Enabled
P0 SAFE_EMERGENCY_HOLD 1 0.05 2 (CRIT_ONLY) true
P1 SAFE_THROTTLE_STRICT 2 0.08 1 (THROTTLE_BULK) true
P2 BALANCED_CONSERVATIVE 4 0.10 0 (ACCEPT_ALL) true
P3 BALANCED_AGILE_FOCUS 6 0.12 0 (ACCEPT_ALL) true
P4 STANDARD_SPRAY_FOCUS 6 0.15 0 (ACCEPT_ALL) false
P5 EXPLORE_AGILE_SPRAY 8 0.15 0 (ACCEPT_ALL) true
P6 HIGH_SPRAY_BACKPRESSURE 10 0.15 0 (ACCEPT_ALL) true
P7 HIGH_SPRAY_OPEN 12 0.30 0 (ACCEPT_ALL) false

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Profile parameters gate three actuators: - Spray quota L_i: max bulk token spread per hop (computeRelaySplit sets floor((nrofCopies - 1) / 2) bounded by active profile L). - Gradient forwarding guard (allowNonDirectBulkForward): when bpEnabled == true, blocks non-destination BULK_ relay if Q_nbr > Q_local - bpRatio (except direct delivery to destination). - Ingress mode (ing in {0, 1, 2}).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

During dense congestion in M3 (seed 7103, node 53, t = 3300.5 s), RL proposes P6 (HIGH_SPRAY_BACKPRESSURE, L=10), Shield rule S3 sets bitmask 11111100 (blocking P6, P7), and safely clamps execution to P3 (BALANCED_AGILE_FOCUS, L=6).

Mechanism 07: Declarative State-Based Rule (SRL) Parser & Predicate Expression Tree

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Allows operators to express autonomic policies in human-readable .txt files (12 non-comment lines in rules_vdtn.txt) without writing, compiling, or redeploying router Java code.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Hard-coded if/else in Java (EnergyAwareEpidemicRouter, 394 LOC): Zero portability across substrates or scenarios; cannot accept dynamic remote updates.
  • External scripting runtime (Lua/JS): Adds JVM serialization complexity and non-deterministic garbage collection overhead.
  • Selected declarative clause evaluator (PredicateExpression + DtnmaRuleParser): Lightweight pure Java, deterministic double comparisons, instant [EDD(val) op thresh -> TRUE/FALSE] strings for ARI logs.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Scenario rule file (Group.rulesFile / DtnmaRouter.rulesFile) -> DtnmaRuleParser.parseRulesFile(...) -> Compiles each RULE: <ARI> | PRIORITY: <int> | DESC: <text> + IF: <clauses> + THEN: CTRL_SET_* block into a priority-sorted list of StateBasedRule objects.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Group.rulesFile / DtnmaRouter.rulesFile (scenarios/rules_vdtn.txt, experimental scenarios/rules_uav.txt); comparisons (>, <, >=, <=, ==, !=), && conjunction or || disjunction, and 4 ControlAction setters (CTRL_SET_SPRAY_QUOTA, CTRL_SET_INGRESS_MODE, CTRL_SET_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL, CTRL_SET_BACKPRESSURE).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Flat clause expression structure (DtnmaRuleParser.java:117-137): - Conjunction (&&): evaluates all (EDD op threshold) clauses (all match -> true). - Disjunction (||): evaluates clauses when ifClause.contains("||") (any match -> true). During evaluate(...) (PredicateExpression.java:31-49): evaluates every clause without short-circuiting so audit logs show full [EDD(val) op thresh -> TRUE/FALSE] provenance (Math.abs(a - b) < 1e-6 for ==).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/PredicateExpression.java:1-145
  • src/routing/StateBasedRule.java:1-81
  • src/routing/DtnmaRuleParser.java:59-165

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

Every matched SRL rule emits its ARI://DTNMA/SRL/<RULE_ID> header and full clause trace into DtnmaAuditReport column 21.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Rules cannot mix nested && and || inside a single IF: clause (|| switches the whole rule to disjunction mode, DtnmaRuleParser.java:120). Missing file paths throw IOException explicitly (:41); rules are sorted descending by priority on load (:113).

9. Worked Mini-Example

scenarios/rules_vdtn.txt: RULE: ARI://DTNMA/SRL/VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE | PRIORITY: 80 | DESC: ... IF: (EDD_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.88) && (EDD_QUEUE_DRIFT >= 0.008) THEN: CTRL_SET_SPRAY_QUOTA(2); CTRL_SET_INGRESS_MODE(1); CTRL_SET_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL(300); CTRL_SET_BACKPRESSURE(true) Evaluated on seed 7103 at t = 3360.5 s: [EDD_QUEUE_RATIO(0.92) >= 0.88 -> TRUE] AND [EDD_QUEUE_DRIFT(0.01) >= 0.01 -> TRUE].

Mechanism 08: Priority Resolution, Hysteresis Latch & Overlay Supersession

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Prevents rapid profile flip-flopping (thrashing) when an EDD hovers near a threshold (e.g., Q \approx 0.88), and lets temporary remote Manager overlays cleanly supersede local rules without permanent lock-in.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Stateless single-step matching: Switches between P1 and P4 every 30 s whenever one packet arrives/departs around threshold boundaries.
  • Explicit separate hysteresis dead-band table: Doubles rule authoring verbosity.
  • Selected priority-preemptible time latch (LATCH <s> + PRIO <p>): Holds an action for latchDurationSec unless a strictly higher-priority hazard fires (e.g., PRIO 100 Emergency Hold preempts PRIO 85 Surge).

3. Architecture & Data Flow

In DtnmaAgent.evaluateAutonomyEngine(...) (DtnmaAgent.java:634-733): 1. Purge expired overlay (now > overlayExpire). 2. Scan candidate rules (overlay slot + local SRL rules) sorted descending by PRIO. 3. Select first matching rule r^*; if no rule matches or active latch holds higher priority and hasn't expired (now < latchUntil), retain latched state.

4. Inputs & Configuration

LATCH <double sec> (typically 60.0–180.0 s in rules_vdtn.txt), PRIO <int> (local 10–99, remote overlay dtnmaControlPriority = 100).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Let rmatch be highest-priority rule evaluating true at time t, and (platch, alatch, tuntil) the active latch state: - If rmatch exists and (t ≥ tuntil OR rmatch.prio > platch): adopt rmatch, set tuntil = t + rmatch.latchSec. - Otherwise if t < tuntil: sustain latched profile with provenance ARI://DTNMA/LATCH/<RULE_ID> (replayable deterministically!).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:634-733 (evaluateAutonomyEngine), :1260-1323 (upsertDownlinkOverlayRule)
  • scenarios/rules_vdtn.txt:1-25

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

Logs exact latch preemption and active rule ARI in DtnmaAuditReport; verify_audit_replay verifies latch continuity across 100.00% of logged epochs.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

PRIORITY: 10 catch-all rules (IF: (EDD_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.0)) provide deterministic recovery backstops in rules_vdtn.txt so nodes never remain stuck throttled after congestion subsides (missing in unvalidated rules_uav.txt).

9. Worked Mini-Example

On node 94 (seed 7103, t = 29460.5 s), VDTN_BUFFER_CRITICAL (PRIO 100) preempts lower-priority states immediately when EDD_ENERGY_SOC(0.19) < 0.20, locking P0 (SAFE_EMERGENCY_HOLD) with ARI://DTNMA/SRL/VDTN_BUFFER_CRITICAL.

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze). Earlier Event A regressions traced to excessive latch windows (> 300 s) holding P1 stale; tuned in v1.0 to 90–180 s.

11. Supervisor Rationale

Essential for finite-state oscillation damping without sacrificing sub-minute critical escalation.

Mechanism 09: Deterministic Hard Safety Shield (S1–S4 + Liveness)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Guarantees hard operational safety invariants (battery reserve, critical buffer starvation, dense radio storm collapse, remote min-safety constraints) regardless of whether the proposal came from SRL, stale latches, or an exploratory M3 RL action.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • RL Reward Penalties Alone (CMDP soft Lagrangian): Allowed 41% critical occupancy during early unshielded learning (P6/P7 storm exploration) before lambda could converge.
  • Selected Mandatory Bitmask Filter (DtnmaSafetyShield): Constructs an 8-bit admissibility vector mask[0..7] analytically before every action executes.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Proposed Profile a_prop + 11 EDDs -> DtnmaSafetyShield.computeAdmissibleMask(...) applies intersection (AND) of constraints S1, S2, S3, S4 + unconditional Liveness mask[0] = true -> If mask[a_prop] == false, maps down safely to highest admissible index <= a_prop (OVERRIDE)!

4. Inputs & Configuration

DtnmaConfig.java: shieldEnabled, shieldCongestionQueue (0.88 or 0.94 mode-dependent), shieldCriticalQueueHigh (0.50), shieldEnergyMin (0.20 default, 0.25 in M0c/M0e-25/remote V1 wave), shieldDensityThreshold (5.0).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

mask = [true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true]
S1 (Critical Buffer):
  if CritQ >= 0.50 or (Q >= 0.94 and dQ >= 0.015): allow {0} only
  else if CritQ >= 0.35 or (Q >= 0.82 and dQ > 0.015): allow {0, 1, 2}
S2 (Battery Survival):
  if SoC < shieldEnergyMin (e.g. 0.20): allow {0, 1}
S3 (Dense Storm Block):
  if Q >= 0.78 and Dens >= 5.0: block {6, 7}
S4 (Remote SRL Clamp, when active prio >= 100):
  block any profile violating overlay maxQuota or minIngress
Liveness Guarantee:
  mask[0] = true  // P0 SAFE_EMERGENCY_HOLD is NEVER masked out

Fallback mapping on OVERRIDE: asafe = max { j ∈ {0..7} : mask[j] ∧ j ≤ aprop } (defaulting to 0).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaSafetyShield.java:102-172 (computeAdmissibleMask, enforce)

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

Every intervention flips column 18 from PASS to OVERRIDE, writes exact 8-bit shield_mask (e.g., 11111100), logs ARI://DTNMA/SHIELD/<GUARD_NAME>, and increments shield_interventions in DtnmaRlMetricsReport.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

CritQ surge trap fix: early pilot coupled only Q without checking CritQ >= 0.50, accidentally over-throttling P0 when BULK_ was near zero; adding explicit CritQ thresholds cut idle P0 occupancy from 41% -> 1.8%.

9. Worked Mini-Example

In M3 (seed 7103, t = 3300.5 s, node 53), RL proposes HIGH_SPRAY_BACKPRESSURE (P6), while Q = 0.9298 >= 0.78 and Dens = 12.0 >= 5.0. S3 sets mask = 11111100 (P6/P7 blocked), logging: OVERRIDE | 11111100 | ARI://DTNMA/SHIELD/DENSE_STORM_GUARD | SHIELD_OVERRIDE(HIGH_SPRAY_BACKPRESSURE->BALANCED_AGILE_FOCUS) (actually down to P3 via composite rule/RL clamped order!).

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze). Directly tested across multiple shield unit checks (Test14–Test18).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Satisfies RFC 7575 Sec 4 bounds: learning or rule bugs never crash the safety envelope.

Mechanism 10: Critical Delivery Protection & Delayed ACK Copy Pruning

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Protects mission-critical dispatches until verified delivery, while circulating lightweight 4 B/ID acknowledgment digests across contacts so nodes reclaim wasted duplicate buffer space automatically.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • No ACKs: Critical copies sit at Tier 4 protection forever until TTL expires (hours), starving fresh traffic.
  • Immediate global erasure via simulator cheat: Breaks DTN realism; violates causality.
  • Selected store-and-sync contact ACK exchange: Mimics real DTN custody/ACK pruning bounded at 32 IDs / contact (4 B each = <= 128 B).

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Destination delivers CRIT_ bundle -> Adds msgId to local deliveredAckSet (512-entry LRU) -> Upon changedConnection contact, exchanges up to 32 ACK IDs with peer -> Peer deletes matching un-sent duplicate copies and promotes any active/evicted ones to Tier 1 deliveredAckSet.

4. Inputs & Configuration

DtnmaContactBeacon.ACK_ID_BYTES = 4, ACK_CACHE_SIZE = 512, ACK_MAX_PER_CONTACT = 32 (DtnmaAgent.java:520-550), dtnmaEnableAckPruning (true across Tiers 1–3).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Bandwidth overhead per contact: BACK = 4 · min(|ΔACK|, 32) ≤ 128\ bytes, billed accurately to control overhead counters alongside 16 B beacons.

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:520-550 (exchangeDeliveryAcks)
  • src/routing/DtnmaContactBeacon.java:18-21

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

critical_buffer_dropped_acked (harmless pruned copies) separated cleanly from unique_critical_lost (real loss) inside DtnmaRlMetricsReport.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

LRU bound (512 IDs) bounds RAM overhead per node; active transfers (isSending) wait until transfer finishes before deletion.

9. Worked Mini-Example

Across 11 seeds of CompA Blackout on ManagedEpidemicRouter, Tier 1 (Protection + ACK pruning) achieves 0 unique critical loss (same 53-style duplicate prunes occur safely in smoke test), proving protection works independently of throughput controls.

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Provides verifiable critical survivability at negligible control byte cost (<= 128 B/contact).

Mechanism 11: Atomic Decision Snapshot, ARI Audit Logging & 100% Replay Verification

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Eliminates "why did node 53 throttle at t = 3360 s?" mysteries and earlier replay mismatches caused by reading post-actuation buffer ratios instead of pre-decision inputs.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • End-of-tick telemetry dumping: Caused tiny (~0.1%) replay mismatches because buffer arrivals inside the same tick altered Q after the rule fired.
  • Selected atomic pre-decision capture + 16-column ARI audit log: Locks eddSnapshot[11] synchronously before evaluating SRL/RL/Shield, writing exact deterministic provenance.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

DtnmaAgent.evaluateAutonomyEngine captures atomic double[11] EDD array -> Evaluates rule -> Applies shield -> Pushes AuditRecord to registered listeners (DtnmaAuditReport) -> Offline Python verifier (verify_audit_replay in evaluate_autonomic_framework.py) re-runs rule & shield parser against logged columns 5–11.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Configured by Report.reportN registration (DtnmaAuditReport), emits # AUDIT_SUMMARY footer + fixed 16-column TSV trace (timestamp, nodeId, decisionId, ...).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Offline verification asserts per logged row r: Parse(r.EDDs, ruleset) ≡ r.ARI \quad ∧ \quad Shield(r.EDDs, r.proposed) ≡ (r.shielded, r.mask)

  • src/report/DtnmaAuditReport.java:1-137

log_bytes_per_node_hour: 28,198.7 B (Stress mean) / 29,906.6 B (Benign mean); 27,099,616 total rows audited across 176 CompB runs with 100.00% exact replay across static ARI (7,917,654 rows) and RL shield masks (3,908,964 rows).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

DtnmaAuditReport checks row headers & warmup filtering (warmupTime); audit snapshots record float precision (%.9f in log vs IEEE double) — atomic ordering prevents rounding from ever diverging across 27M+ rows.

Row from seed 7103 M2 stress audit log (t = 3360.5 s, node 53): 3360.5 3360.5 53 M2_AUTONOMIC_SRL 0.919217000 0.005594100 ... SAFE_THROTTLE_STRICT PASS 11111111 ARI://DTNMA/SRL/VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE — replayed deterministically offline with 0 discrepancies.

Mechanism 12: DtnmaManagedRouter Thin-Adapter Composition Contract

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Establishes a single router-agnostic Java interface decoupling forwarding substrates from DtnmaAgent, avoiding O(R) duplication of 2,095 lines of management logic across every routing protocol.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Subclass inheritance (EnergyAwareEpidemicRouter, 394 LOC): Re-implements EDD tracking, ACKs, and thresholds inside every router subclass; drifts easily when policies change.
  • Selected composition interface (DtnmaManagedRouter + DtnmaAgent): Any ONE ActiveRouter delegates lifecycle hooks (update, createNewMessage, checkReceiving, makeRoomForMessage, changedConnection) via ~253.5 mean non-comment LOC.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Router Adapter (extends StockRouter implements DtnmaManagedRouter) owns one private final DtnmaAgent agent -> Exposes 15 buffer/connection/energy getters + 4 actuator setters (setDynamicSprayQuota, setIngressMode, setRoutineTelemetryInterval, setBackpressureEnabled) -> Delegates forwarding filters cleanly to agent.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Configured automatically inside router copy constructor; supportsDynamicControlReconfig() returns true; copies clone cleanly in ONE's replicate() prototype pattern.

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Interface contract guarantees invariance: - getBufferOccupancyRatio() = (Btotal - Bfree) / Btotal - getCriticalOccupancyRatio() = \summ ∈ CRIT |m| / Btotal - getEnergySoc() = clamp(Erem / Einit, 0, 1) - createNewMessage(m) wraps agent.evaluateCreateNewMessage(m) cleanly before calling super.createNewMessage(m).

  • src/routing/DtnmaManagedRouter.java:1-46
  • src/routing/ManagedEpidemicRouter.java:21-98

Agent attaches identically to all adapters, enabling unified DtnmaAuditReport and DtnmaRlMetricsReport emission across heterogeneous protocols.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze). Replaces earlier monolithic routing hierarchy cleanly.

Core architectural contribution of ADTNM (2,095 shared core LOC vs 253.5 mean adapter LOC).

Mechanism 13: Substrate-Specific Relay Adaptations (SnW, PRoPHETv2, MaxProp, Epidemic)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Applies priority ordering (CRIT_/CTRL_ before BULK_), backpressure blocking (allowNonDirectBulkForward), and Tier 3 copy quotas without corrupting each router's native path-selection estimator.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Replacing native comparators globally: Destroys PRoPHET delivery predictability (P(a,b)) and MaxProp Dijkstra cost ordering.
  • Selected Tiered Native Wrapping: Sorts candidate tuples into CRIT_/CTRL_ first, then applies native router comparator inside each priority band + optional Tier 3 replica cap.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

In each Managed*Router: - ManagedSprayAndWaitRouter: Clamps binary token splitting (MSG_COUNT_PROPERTY) dynamically under Tier 3 when active profile quota L_i < defaultQuota. - ManagedProphetV2Router: Updates native RFC 6693 aging/transitivity untouched; filters BULK_ relays via allowNonDirectBulkForward and priority-orders tryAllMessages. - ManagedMaxPropRouter: Keeps Dijkstra encounter probabilities and cost tables untouched; guards congestion & ACKed duplicate eviction cleanly. - ManagedEpidemicRouter: Retains unrestricted flooding under nominal P4, throttling bulk flooding smoothly under S1–S4 and ingress guards (14.5 -> 125.9 survival jump in CompA Blackout).

4. Inputs & Configuration

dtnmaInterventionTier: TIER1_PROTECTION_ONLY, TIER2_PROTECTION_INGRESS_ENERGY, TIER3_FULL_WITH_REPLICA_CAPS; stock router settings (SprayAndWaitRouter.nrofCopies = 6, ProphetV2Router.secondsInTimeUnit = 30).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Tier gating inside DtnmaAgent: - If Tier == 1: skip ingress throttling, backpressure block, and dynamic spray cap — preserve Priority* behavior cleanly. - If Tier == 2: enable ingressMode + S1–S4 + SRL rules (L cap bypassed). - If Tier == 3: enforce full profile (L_i, bp, ing).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/ManagedSprayAndWaitRouter.java:1-291
  • src/routing/ManagedProphetV2Router.java:1-291
  • src/routing/ManagedMaxPropRouter.java:1-350
  • src/routing/ManagedEpidemicRouter.java:1-236

Tracked identically across all 4 routers in compA_vdtn_overload, compA_energy_blackout, compA_benign, and compA_tiers.

Tier 1 leaves Epidemic unprotected against battery drain (14.5/126 alive in Blackout), isolating why Tier 2 (125.9/126 alive) drives survival while Tier 3 adds minimal marginal gain (0 extra alive nodes on Epidemic/SnW).

Mechanism 14: Remote Manager Overlay (CTRL_UPDATE_ / CTRL_GROUP_) & Rule Upsert

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Allows a central DTN Manager to issue time-bounded configuration waves (such as tightening the battery survival threshold to shieldEnergyMin = 0.25) over opportunistic DTN links without rebooting agents.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Permanent global overwrite: Locks agents permanently into defensive throttling even long after a scenario window closes.
  • Selected priority-100 overlay slot (upsertDownlinkOverlayRule): Temporary highest-priority rule overriding PRIO <= 99 local rules until expiration or explicit NOMINAL release.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Manager host generates CTRL_ bundle carrying command property -> Routed across DTN relays to target nodes (unicast or group-flood) -> On reception at applyDownlinkControlBundle (DtnmaAgent.java:1200-1323), node records adoption latency (downlink_t90_sec), installs overlay rule at PRIO = 100, and updates shieldEnergyMin / throttle bounds when instructed.

4. Inputs & Configuration

dtnmaControlPriority = 100, dtnmaControlTimeoutSec, message prefix CTRL_UPDATE_ (targeted) or CTRL_GROUP_ (shared wave); payload specifies profile clamp, energy floor, or nominal release.

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Wave Adoption CDF fraction at offset τ ≥ 0 after wave issue t_0: Fwave(τ) = \frac{|{i ∈ Targets : trx, i - t_0 ≤ τ}|}{|Targets|} Sampled across [0, 60] one-minute bins (q10, q25, q50, q75, q90, q95) into # WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF.

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:1200-1323 (applyDownlinkControlBundle, upsertDownlinkOverlayRule)
  • src/report/DtnmaRlMetricsReport.java:1229-1266 (# WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF computation)

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

Logs wave percentiles, downlink_t90_sec, and total_ctrl_tx_J. Reporting Note: When 0 waves are received (e.g., M2 in groupflood), downlink_t90_sec records an end-of-horizon sentinel (30849.0) while downlink_90pct_reached = 0.0.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Duplicate remote wave copies are deduplicated cleanly by message ID; remote overlays never drop P0 liveness admissibility (S1–S2 safety guards stay active).

In compB_exp_controls_stress (seed 7211), M1-U's CTRL_UPDATE_THROTTLE_W1_ wave issued at 3601 s hits 50% node adoption at 1131 s (~18.9 min) and 90% (T90) at 2722 s (~45.4 min) — completely missing the 300 s Event A surge!

Mechanism 15: Unicast (M1-U) vs. Legacy Flood (M1-F) vs. Group Flood (M1-F-Group) Dissemination

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Isolates control transport physics from decision intelligence: separates whether delayed remote management fails because of unicast queueing (M1-U), excessive per-node flood storm (M1-F), or fundamental speed-of-light / contact delay (M1-F-Group).

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • M1-U (DtnmaM1RemoteRouter): Sends N = 120 separate unicast CTRL_UPDATE_ bundles (one per managed node).
  • M1-F (DtnmaM1FloodRouter, confirmatory v1.0): Floods all 120 individual CTRL_UPDATE_ bundles epidemics-style (118.7 kJ radio cost -> 13.55/126 survivors!).
  • M1-F-Group (DtnmaM1FloodGroupRouter, exploratory v1.0-exp-controls): Floods 1 shared group-addressed CTRL_GROUP_ bundle per wave adopted by every node (201.6 J cost, T90 = 841 s, 99.5/126 survivors).

3. Architecture & Data Flow

compB_multitimescale vs compB_exp_groupflood_*: In M1-F-Group, receiving a single CTRL_GROUP_ bundle triggers local overlay adoption at that host and continues propagating the single bundle to peers until TTL expires.

4. Inputs & Configuration

Configured via scenario message generators (CTRL_UPDATE_* vs CTRL_GROUP_*) and mode class selection (DtnmaM1RemoteRouter, DtnmaM1FloodRouter, DtnmaM1FloodGroupRouter).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Control transmission energy breakdown: Ectrl, tx = \sumtx ∈ CTRL Ptx · \frac{|msg|}{baud} ⇒ \begin{cases} 118,728\ J & (M1-F: O(N^2)\ per-node floods) \ 2,512\ J & (M1-U: unicast) \ 201.6\ J & (M1-F-Group: O(N)\ single-copy group flood) \end{cases}

total_ctrl_tx_J, downlink_t90_sec, alive_nodes_end, and per-wave CDFs (# WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Reviewer critique caught M1-F (118.7 kJ) as a strawman control channel prior to exploratory follow-up; adding M1-F-Group (201.6 J) fairly evaluates best-case remote flooding!

With single-copy CTRL_GROUP_THROTTLE_W1_ (seed 7211), M1-F-Group hits T50 = 441.5 s (T90 = 823.0 s across Wave 1) at tiny energy cost, saving 99.5/126 nodes across 12h stress — still too slow (441.5 s > 300 s) to prevent Event A stale throttling (252 s for 10%, median ~483 s across 11 seeds).

Mechanism 17: Compact 16 B Contact Beacon & Peer Queue Gradient Exchange

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Supplies neighbors with real-time congestion awareness (Q_nbr, CritQ_nbr, SoC_nbr) upon wireless contact without transmitting heavy XML/JSON routing state dumps.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Periodic broadcast flooding of node state tables: Saturated channel under high density (>= 12 neighbors in storm hubs).
  • Selected unicast contact 16 B beacon (DtnmaContactBeacon): Piggybacks O(1) state bytes on peer handshake every >= 5.0 s.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

changedConnection UP event -> Check cooldown (>= 5.0 s) -> Peer writes 16 B beacon (Q, CritQ, SoC, active profile, timestamp) -> EddTelemetrySampler updates EDD_NEIGHBOR_MIN_QUEUE and EDD_NEIGHBOR_QUEUE_GRAD = Q_local - Q_nbr_min -> Backpressure forwarder uses peer Q_nbr.

4. Inputs & Configuration

DtnmaContactBeacon.java:18-21: BEACON_SIZE_BYTES = 16, ACK_ID_BYTES = 4, GOSSIP_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 648 (M3 only).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

  • EDD_NEIGHBOR_MIN_QUEUE: minj ∈ FreshNbrs(t) Q_j, where freshness respects stale timeout window (300 s).
  • Backpressure forwarding rule (allowNonDirectBulkForward): block transit BULK_ relay to peer j if Q_j > Qlocal - bpratio or peer j is battery-depleted (SoC_j < minSoC).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaContactBeacon.java:1-100
  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:520-550, :1119-1159

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

beacon_overhead_bytes and control_bytes_total in DtnmaRlMetricsReport. Even across heavy 12 h runs, beacon + ACK bytes account for << 1% of total payload traffic (control_to_payload_ratio).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

EnergyAwareEpidemicRouter replicates a 5.0 s cooldown beacon cache internally so baseline A3 parity isolates policy from transport overhead.

9. Worked Mini-Example

When node 53 hits Q = 0.92 (P1, bpRatio = 0.08), if its neighbor reports Q_nbr = 0.90 via its 16 B beacon, 0.90 > 0.92 - 0.08 (= 0.84) -> Backpressure blocks non-direct BULK_ upload, sparing the congested peer while still delivering bundles addressed directly to that peer (dest == peer).

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Enables distributed congestion backpressure (VDTN_NEIGHBOR_RELIEF) and energy relief at fixed 16 B wire budget per handshake.

Mechanism 18: Shielded Linear CMDP Q-Learning Agent (M3, Implemented, experimental)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Explores whether a lightweight online reinforcement learning planner (ShieldedCmdpRlAgent) choosing across P0..P7 can adapt dynamically to unforeseen traffic shifts better than static rules (M2). Empirical finding (v1.0): It did not (bulk 63.0% vs 66.0% stress, 79.8% vs 82.0% benign, 76.0 vs 83.8 alive nodes).

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Deep Q-Network (PyTorch / JNI): Fails determinism, memory, and pure-Java ONE execution constraints.
  • Unshielded linear SARSA/Q-learning: Triggered 41% critical occupancy surges during early unconstrained exploration (P6/P7 storms).
  • Selected Shielded 20-Feature Linear Q-Agent: Learns wReward[8][20] weights over normalized EDD features while restricting action selection strictly to mask[a] == true from DtnmaSafetyShield.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Every 30 s -> Extract double[20] feature vector phi -> Query DtnmaSafetyShield for 8-bit mask -> Compute Q(s, a) = wreward[a] · φ for admissible actions -> ε-greedy selection over admissible set -> Execute profile -> On next epoch compute shaped reward r_t (computeLocalEpochRewardCost) & TD(0) update.

4. Inputs & Configuration

ShieldedCmdpRlAgent.java:20-80, DtnmaConfig.java: rlAlpha = 0.05, rlGamma = 0.90, rlEpsilonInit = 0.15, rlEpsilonMin = 0.02, rlEpsilonDecay = 0.995, rlWeightClip = 10.0. isAutonomicRlMode = true in M3.

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

  • Linear action-value function (NUM_FEATURES = 20, HAZARD_FEATURE_INDICES = {6, 15, 16, 17}): Q(s, a) = \sumk=0^{19} wa, k φ_k(s), \qquad a ∈ {0..7} : mask[a] = true
  • Safe TD(0) update: \delta_t = r_t + γ maxa' : mask[a'] Q(s', a') - Q(s, a_t), \qquad wa_t, k ≤ftarrow clip\big(wa_t, k + α \delta_t φ_k(s),\ [-10, 10]\big)
  • Local shaped epoch reward (DtnmaAgent.java:822-854): combines critical & bulk delivery increments, congestion overshoot penalty, and battery drain penalty (re-tuned to remove earlier -20 voluntary P0 hold distortions).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/ShieldedCmdpRlAgent.java:1-294
  • src/routing/DtnmaAgent.java:822-854 (computeLocalEpochRewardCost)

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

rl_avg_reward, rl_avg_cost, shield_interventions, shield_greedy_override_rate; audit rows log SHIELDED_CMDP_RL + exact 11111100 mask on every override.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

Weight explosion prevented via hard [-10.0, 10.0] clipping; shield mask[0] = true ensures random ε-exploration never chooses lethal starvation states.

9. Worked Mini-Example

At t = 3300.5 s (seed 7103, node 53), M3 chooses greedy/exploratory P6 (HIGH_SPRAY_BACKPRESSURE). S3 overrides (11111100) down to BALANCED_AGILE_FOCUS, logging ARI://DTNMA/SHIELD/DENSE_STORM_GUARD — keeping zero critical loss (0 unique lost across 11 seeds) even though cumulative bulk & survival lag behind M2.

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented, experimental (v1.0-freeze). Honest negative: Underperformed hand-written SRL (M2) on every stress and benign endpoint (H3/CompB).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Open research question: Demonstrates safety shielding protects critical traffic even under weak learned policies, while honestly showing hand-crafted domain rules outperform shallow online Q-learning in v1.0.

Mechanism 19: Symmetric RL Weight Gossip & Retired Primal-Dual lambda = 0

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Shares learned Q-weights (wReward[8][20]) across opportunistic contacts (gossipMergeSymmetric) so cold-start nodes benefit from peer experience, while recording why dynamic primal-dual lambda updates were retired prior to v1.0.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Asymmetric overwrite: Slow nodes overwrite well-trained hubs.
  • Primal-dual soft Lagrangian penalty (lambda > 0): Oscillated wildly during multi-timescale traffic bursts and still permitted 41% critical occupancy before lambda caught up.
  • Selected bounded symmetric gossip (648 B payload) + lambda = 0.0 (Deprecated or removed dynamic multiplier): Uses DtnmaSafetyShield strictly for hard constraints while gossipMergeSymmetric blends weight tables safely on contact.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Peer contact opens (M3 only) -> Serialize 8 x 20 float matrix + header (8 * 20 * 4 + 8 = 648 B, GOSSIP_PAYLOAD_BYTES) -> Merge symmetrically with blending coefficient rlGossipAlpha -> Log gossip bytes into control_bytes_total.

4. Inputs & Configuration

DtnmaContactBeacon.GOSSIP_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 648; DtnmaConfig.java:63-66 & scenarios/dtnma_params_default.txt:29-32: rlLambdaInit = 0.0, rlEtaLambda = 0.0, rlTargetCost = 0.30, rlLambdaMax = 5.0 (backward-compatibility shims).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Symmetric weight blend between local W^{(i)} and peer W^{(j)}: W^{(i)}new = (1 - ηg) W^{(i)} + ηg W^{(j)}, \qquad λ ≡ 0.0\ (fixed) Because λ ≡ 0, getLagrangianValue(a, phi) (ShieldedCmdpRlAgent.java:136) returns pure wreward[a] · φ.

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/ShieldedCmdpRlAgent.java:29, 136, :295-356 (gossipMergeSymmetric)
  • src/routing/DtnmaContactBeacon.java:18-21

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

gossip_overhead_bytes folded into control_bytes_total.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

HAZARD_FEATURE_INDICES = {6, 15, 16, 17} receive dedicated sign/clip stabilization during gossip updates. Zero NaN/Inf permitted (Double.isFinite guard).

9. Worked Mini-Example

Two M3 taxis meet after 1 hour (648 B exchanged); instead of resetting exploration, the isolated node immediately incorporates peer congestion weights around density/queue gradient indices.

10. Status Label & Evolution

  • Symmetric Gossip: Implemented, experimental (M3 only).
  • Primal-Dual Dynamic lambda Adaptation: Deprecated or removed (lambda = 0.0, compatibility keys kept for older config loading).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Preserves full scientific memory so newcomers understand why getLagrangianValue() exists in source while lambda remains 0.0.

Mechanism 20: Static Benchmark Controls (M0b, M0c, M0d, M0e-20, M0e-25)

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Eliminates strawman comparisons! Instead of comparing adaptive management only against an unmanaged stock router (M0a), static controls bracket protection alone, pre-installed guards, permanent caution, and fixed energy cutoffs.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

Only testing M0a vs M2 fails reviewer scrutiny ("would pre-installing the shield statically work just as well?"). These 5 static baselines isolate every individual policy mechanism cleanly.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Lightweight wrapper subclasses override DtnmaConfig flags inside copy constructors (P4, shieldEnabled, shieldEnergyMin, P1 static): - M0b (DtnmaM0bStaticRouter): Protection + ACK pruning only (P4, no congestion/energy shield). - M0c (DtnmaM0cV1GuardRouter): Pre-installed V1 guard (shieldEnergyMin = 0.25, Q <= 0.88, static throttle). - M0d (DtnmaM0dConservativeRouter): Always conservative P1 (L = 2, INGRESS_THROTTLE_BULK) from t = 0. - M0e-20 / M0e-25 (DtnmaM0eEnergy20/25Router): Exploratory SoC cutoff (0.20 or 0.25) with zero congestion rules (v1.0-exp-controls).

4. Inputs & Configuration

Hard-coded config presets per mode router (DtnmaM0*Router.java) evaluated on identical SEEDS_11 (7103..7207 confirmatory; 7211..7307 exploratory).

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

Mode matrix invariance guarantees identical forwarding & control byte baselines so paired differences (M2 - M0*) measure strictly policy effects (df = 10 paired t-test).

6. Code Anchors

  • src/routing/DtnmaM0bStaticRouter.java, DtnmaM0cV1GuardRouter.java, DtnmaM0dConservativeRouter.java
  • src/routing/DtnmaM0eEnergy20Router.java:1-48, DtnmaM0eEnergy25Router.java:1-48

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

M0c achieves 126/126 stress survival at severe benign throughput penalty (53.9% vs 82.0% M2, confirming H4); M0e-25 ties M2 stress survival (83.8/126, p = 1.0).

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

M0b keeps 0 unique critical loss (Protection works!) yet collapses to 54.1/126 survivors in 12h Stress because it lacks S2 energy throttling.

9. Worked Mini-Example

Comparing M0e-20 (73.7 alive) -> M2-LocalOnly (80.0 alive) -> M0e-25 (83.8 alive) -> M2 (83.8 alive) reveals cleanly in seconds how much M2's end-of-mission node survival relies on 0.25 vs 0.20 SoC threshold!

10. Status Label & Evolution

M0b..M0d: Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze); M0e-20/25: Implemented+tested (v1.0-exp-controls).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Makes thesis claims falsifiable against non-strawman competitors.

Mechanism 21: Three-Tier Reporting Pipeline & Per-Event Cohort / Horizon Tracking

1. Purpose & Problem Solved

Fixes right-censoring and whole-mission cancellation artifacts! Whole-12h averages hide short 300 s burst collapses (Event A), so DtnmaRlMetricsReport tracks per-event creation cohorts over fixed post-window horizons.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

  • Global run averages (MessageStatsReport only): Cancels early surge drops (3600–3900 s) against hours of subsequent recovery traffic.
  • Unbounded cohort horizon: Messages born at t = 28700 s near end-of-run (36000 s) vs t = 3650 s get unequal delivery windows.
  • Selected Fixed-Horizon Event Cohorts (Event A, B, C): Simulation runs cleanly through endTime >= t_end + horizon (43200 s vs 28800 + 3600 s) eliminating right-censoring!

3. Architecture & Data Flow

DtnmaRlMetricsReport registers MessageListener + UpdateListener (DtnmaRlMetricsReport.java:41-90, 763-776, 1175-1270): tags each bundle upon creation with event bitmask (A: 3600–3900 s, B: 7200–9000 s, C: 21600–28800 s, horizon +3600 s), samples energy/queue/throttle every update tick, and emits Tier 1–4 summary + event{A,B,C}_* blocks.

4. Inputs & Configuration

reportN = DtnmaRlMetricsReport, FAULT_ONSET_SEC = 7200.0, FAULT_END_SEC = 14400.0, AOI_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SEC = 10.0.

5. Algorithm & Exact Math / Equations

  • Cohort delivery (computeCohortDelivery, :763-776): cohort_deliv(W) = \frac{|{m : tcreate(m) ∈ [tstart^W, tend^W) ∧ deliv(m) ∧ (tdeliv - tcreate ≤ H)}|}{|{m : tcreate(m) ∈ [tstart^W, tend^W)}|}
  • Normalized congestion stress (nodesec_q90): \frac{1}{N} ∈tt_{start}^{tend} |{i : Q_i(t) ≥ 0.90}|\,dt
  • Normalized stale throttle (stale_throttle_nodesec): node-seconds with ingressMode > 0 after tend^W normalized by N.

6. Code Anchors

  • src/report/DtnmaRlMetricsReport.java:41-90, :701-776, :1175-1271

7. Outputs, Telemetry & Logs

Emits 60+ machine-parseable key: value fields (unique_critical_lost, critical_buffer_dropped, critical_buffer_dropped_acked, eventA_stale_throttle_nodesec, eventC_bulk_deliv, alive_nodes_end, total_ctrl_tx_J, decision_cpu_us_mean) + # WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF rows.

8. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Safeguards

unique_critical_lost counts distinct un-delivered non-TTL critical IDs dropped rather than inflated multi-copy replica drops (whereas DtnmaDecisionReport folds ACK-pruned copies into its summary drop total).

9. Worked Mini-Example

Event C (21600–28800 s) bulk delivery shows why cohort tracking matters (H2): whole-mission bulk differs by -7.0 pp (66% vs 73%), whereas inside the late 2-hour storm Event C cohort (1h horizon), M2 beats M1-U by +19.21 +/- 3.97 pp (p_holm = 1.58e-6, 11/11 seeds) because M1-U's delayed throttle wave stays stuck!

10. Status Label & Evolution

Implemented+tested (v1.0-freeze).

11. Supervisor Rationale

Fixes outcome masking across heterogeneous timescales (Event A = 5 min, B = 30 min, C = 2 h).

Captures 300 s-binned fleet survival trajectories (aliveNodes, avgSoC, cumulative delivery ratio, energy spent) cleanly across 12-hour stress scenarios without bloating multi-gigabyte raw trace logs.

2. Design Alternatives Considered

Logging per-tick per-node battery vectors (126 x 432,000 ticks = tens of MB per run). Aggregated 300 s fleet snapshots produce clean < 15 KB .txt files across 627 urban VDTN runs.

DtnmaRecoveryTimelineReport.updated(...) samples all hosts every 300 s, emits 8-column tab-separated snapshot (time, alive, avgSoc, critDeliv, bulkDeliv, ... , totalEnergyJ, critLost), and appends final snapshot on done().

src/report/DtnmaRecoveryTimelineReport.java:1-260.

Records cumulative energy expenditure Δ E(t) = \sumi=1^N (Einit - E_i(t)) alongside live survival curve Nalive(t).

Mechanism 23: Per-Decision 16-Column ARI Audit Schema (DtnmaAuditReport)

Provides complete machine-verifiable forensic accountability for every single 30 s autonomic decision across every node (~27.1M total rows across CompB).

Free-text System.out debug logging (unparseable, unordered). Strict tabular schema preserves fixed columns for downstream automated verification.

3. Architecture & Data Flow

Registered as One Report; listens to DtnmaAgent decision callbacks; writes # metadata header, TSV decision rows, and # AUDIT_SUMMARY footer summarizing total_audited_decisions, traceable_ari_ratio, shield_overrides, and log_bytes_per_node_hour.

traceable_ari_ratio = \frac{|{rows starting with \texttt{ARI://DTNMA/}}|}{Ndecisions} ≡ 1.0000.

1. Repository Layout & Package Responsibilities

SUPERVISOR NOTE LOC Accounting (A3 evidence): The 7 core engine classes (DtnmaAgent, DtnmaSafetyShield, EddTelemetrySampler, DtnmaRuleParser, PredicateExpression, ControlAction, StateBasedRule) total 2,095 non-comment LOC, each Managed*Router thin adapter averages 253.5 LOC, and declarative vDTN rules span just 12 non-comment lines — replacing 394-line hand-coded protocol subclasses like EnergyAwareEpidemicRouter.

2. Boot-to-Decision Execution Lifecycle Inside The ONE

Every simulation instantiates one prototype router per host group via Settings reflection, cloning per-node state via replicate():

DTNSim.main -> SimScenario parses dtnma_params_default.txt + scenario.txt
  -> Host group calls router.replicate() -> constructs Managed*Router(prototype)
     -> initializes DtnmaConfig (48 fields) & compiles dtnmaRuleFile via DtnmaRuleParser
  -> Loop every dt_tick = 0.1 s until endTime:
     1. World moves nodes -> NetworkInterface checks proximity -> changedConnection(con)
        -> DtnmaAgent.onChangedConnection(con)
           -> exchanges 16 B DtnmaContactBeacon (cooldown >= 5.0 s)
           -> exchanges <= 32 ACK IDs (4 B each) -> prunes delivered CRIT_ duplicates
           -> [M3 only] exchanges 648 B ShieldedCmdpRlAgent weights
     2. Router.update() calls DtnmaAgent.onBeforeUpdate(now):
        -> If now - lastEval >= dtnmaTelemetryIntervalSec (30.0 s):
           a. EddTelemetrySampler.sampleAndCompute() captures 11 EDDs atomically
           b. SRL matches prioritized StateBasedRules + hysteresis LATCH / overlay slot
              [or M3 runs ShieldedCmdpRlAgent Q-value + epsilon-greedy]
           c. DtnmaSafetyShield enforces S1..S4 + Liveness mask[0]=true -> ACTIVE profile
           d. Applies L_i, bpRatio, ingressMode, backpressureEnabled to router hooks
           e. Logs atomic 16-col ARI decision row to DtnmaAuditReport listeners
        -> super.update() executes substrate forwarding filtered by:
           - 5-tier tryAllMessages priority queue (CRIT_ -> CTRL_ -> BULK_)
           - allowNonDirectBulkForward(m, peer) backpressure guard
           - Dynamic Tier 3 copy quota clamping (ManagedSprayAndWaitRouter)
     3. Incoming transfer checks: DtnmaAgent.evaluateCheckReceiving -> ByteBudget + Ingress
     4. Buffer full eviction: DtnmaAgent.selectNextMessageToRemove -> 5-tier O(N) scan
  -> End of run: Reports flush MessageStatsReport, DtnmaRlMetricsReport, DtnmaAuditReport

3. Core Dependency DAG & Key Class Contracts

  • Zero Circular Dependencies: DtnmaConfig (POD settings) & ControlAction & DtnmaPolicyProfile -> PredicateExpression -> StateBasedRule -> DtnmaRuleParser -> DtnmaSafetyShield & EddTelemetrySampler & ShieldedCmdpRlAgent -> DtnmaAgent <-> DtnmaManagedRouter (implemented by Managed*Router).
  • Two Separate Composition vs. Standalone Trees:
  • DtnmaRouter (src/routing/DtnmaRouter.java, 700 lines): direct Spray-and-Wait-based router exposing DtnmaM0b..M3 mode presets (DtnmaM0bStaticRouter, DtnmaM0cV1GuardRouter, DtnmaM1RemoteRouter, DtnmaM2SrlRouter, DtnmaM3RlRouter, etc.).
  • Managed*Router (ManagedSprayAndWaitRouter, ManagedProphetV2Router, ManagedMaxPropRouter, ManagedEpidemicRouter): wraps stock ONE routers by implementing DtnmaManagedRouter (src/routing/DtnmaManagedRouter.java:1-46).

4. Safe Extension Recipes (How Do I Extend ADTNM?)

Recipe A: Add a New SRL Policy Without Recompiling Java

  1. Author a RULE: ... / IF: ... / THEN: ... rule block using valid EDD_* names, comparison operators (>, <, >=, <=, ==, !=), && or ||, CTRL_SET_* actuators, and a unique ARI://DTNMA/SRL/... URI.
  2. Always include a low-priority catch-all recovery rule (PRIORITY: 10, e.g., IF: (EDD_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.0)) so nodes release throttling smoothly when congestion subsides.
  3. Point Group.rulesFile and DtnmaRouter.rulesFile to your custom .txt file and verify 100.00% replay via verify_audit_replay.

Recipe B: Wrap Another Stock ONE Router

  1. Subclass StockOneRouter implements DtnmaManagedRouter.
  2. Instantiate private final DtnmaAgent agent in both constructor and copy constructor (safely normalizing initialEnergy, defaulting to 1.0 when mains-powered).
  3. Implement all getters and setters specified in DtnmaManagedRouter.java:1-46, overriding update(), createNewMessage(), checkReceiving(), makeRoomForMessage(), changedConnection(), and prioritizing CRIT_/CTRL_ tuples ahead of native tryAllMessages ordering.
  4. Run DtnmaUnitTests and verify Tier 1 (TIER1_PROTECTION_ONLY) equivalence against a priority-only baseline.

Recipe C: Wire an Existing Auxiliary Telemetry Signal (EDD_ENERGY_DRAIN)

EddTelemetrySampler already computes EDD_ENERGY_DRAIN (EddTelemetrySampler.java:33,204), making it immediately usable in PredicateExpression rules once calibrated against benign multi-contact traffic bursts.

Chapter 6: Scenario Settings, Evaluation Methodology & Empirical Results

Strict Methodological Separation: Quantitative values throughout this chapter trace programmatically to provenance_ledger.json. The frozen Confirmatory Evaluation (v1.0-freeze) comprises 627 held-out urban VDTN runs across eleven prime random seeds (7103–7207) analyzed with Holm–Bonferroni family-wise error control. Subsequent Post-Freeze Exploratory Controls (v1.0-exp-controls) comprise 176 runs over eleven disjoint prime seeds (7211–7307) and are reported separately with unadjusted p-values (p_unadj).

1. Experimental Design Philosophy & Five-Stage Evaluation Pipeline

A recurring pitfall in Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Network (DTN) simulation studies is evaluating a management mechanism on a single traffic burst, an unmatched random seed, or an unverified steady-state average where localized outages wash out. To eliminate these confounding factors, ADTNM enforces a five-stage evaluation pipeline spanning configuration, execution, instrumentation, offline cryptographic-grade replay, and paired inferential statistics:

  1. Declarative Parameterization & Seed Pairing: Every campaign is specified as a deterministic The ONE .txt scenario file using coprime array sweeps (e.g., Group.router = [ModeA; ModeB; ...] crossed with MovementModel.rngSeed = [7103; 7109; ...]). Because MovementModel.rngSeed fixes identical node trajectories, radio contact schedules, initial battery draws, and bundle arrival events across every comparator within a matched seed pair, any measured difference is attributable purely to the management policy rather than stochastic mobility variance.
  2. Headless Multi-Core Execution: tools/parallel_batch_runner.py parses each scenario's sweep Cartesian product (--dry-run verifies run count before execution), validates coprime array geometry, and dispatches isolated core.DTNSim -b 1 JVM processes (1,536 MB heap, discrete tick Scenario.updateInterval = 0.5 s). Runs begin with a 1,000 s spatial mobility warm-up (MovementModel.warmup = 1000) before primary workload telemetry stabilizes.
  3. Four-Stream Report Instrumentation: Each simulated run emits four complementary logs: MessageStatsReport (network-wide delivery, overhead, and latency summaries), DtnmaRlMetricsReport (class-separated delivery, fixed-horizon event cohorts, wave adoption cumulative distribution functions, and control energy), DtnmaRecoveryTimelineReport (300 s-binned fleet health curves), and DtnmaAuditReport (16-column per-decision ARI provenance traces).
  4. Deterministic Offline Audit Replay (R1): Immediately after simulation, verify_audit_replay (tools/evaluate_autonomic_framework.py) re-parses the rule set (rules_vdtn.txt), feeds the atomically captured telemetry columns from every row of DtnmaAuditReport back through the rule and safety shield logic, and checks that every emitted ARI://DTNMA/... identifier and 8-bit safety mask matches bit-for-bit (100.00% verified).
  5. Seed-Clustered Statistical Inference: Rather than treating correlated bundles or nodes within a single simulation as independent observations, metrics are aggregated per seed (n = 11, degrees of freedom df = 10) and evaluated using paired Student's t-tests with 95% confidence intervals (t<sub>0.975, 10</sub> * SE), Hedges' gav effect sizes, step-down Holm–Bonferroni adjustment across the primary confirmatory family (m = 4), and Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) within a ±1.0 percentage-point margin for architectural equivalence.
