3.2 Node Groups, Mobility Models & Radio Interfaces

All confirmatory and exploratory scenarios evaluate Helsinki Urban Vehicular DTN (compA_*, compB_*, 126 Nodes, 4,500 × 3,400 m), where heterogeneous mobile nodes traverse real city street topologies (roads.wkt, main_roads.wkt, pedestrian_paths.wkt, shops.wkt):

  • Pedestrians (Group1, 40 hosts): 0.5–1.5 m/s, waitTime = 0–60 s, ShortestPathMapBasedMovement, single short-range btInterface (250 kbps, 35 m range).
  • City Cars (Group2, 40 hosts): 2.7–13.9 m/s, map-constrained okMaps = 1, btInterface.
  • Delivery / Patrol Vehicles (Group3, 34 hosts): 2.5–11.5 m/s, map-constrained, btInterface.
  • Backbone Trams (Groups 4–6, 6 hosts = 2 + 2 + 2 across tram3.wkt, tram4.wkt, tram10.wkt): Deterministic MapRouteMovement (7–10 m/s), enlarged transit buffers (15 MB in Overload, 30 MB in CompB, 50 MB in Blackout/Benign), and dual radios combining btInterface with highspeedInterface (10 Mbps, 1,000 m range).
  • Autonomous DTNMA Managers (Group7, 6 hosts): Slow mobile ground/road hubs (0.5–1.0 m/s, 300–600 s pause, 100 MB buffer, 500,000 J mains-powered batteries with 0.0 W scan/transmit energy). Host 120 injects remote control policy waves (W1–W3) toward field agents 0–119.

3.3 Radio Energy Budget & Why Blackouts Emerge

In battery-constrained scenarios, radios consume idle discovery power continuously (scanEnergy = 0.05 W in Stress/Blackout; 0.04 W in Benign), scan-response power (0.02 W), and high active transmit/receive power (transmitEnergy = 0.90 W Stress/Blackout; 0.85 W Benign). Over a 12 h (43,200 s) mission, continuous radio scanning alone draws 43,200 × 0.05 = 2,160 J. Because Stress field nodes start with 2,650–3,650 J (4,500–6,000 J in Blackout), each node possesses only 490–1,490 J of surplus transmission budget in Stress. Flooding routers (Epidemic, MaxProp) or unthrottled bulk relays rapidly burn through that margin during burst traffic, knocking nodes offline permanently and breaking multi-hop connectivity.

3.4 Workloads, Stressor Cohorts (Events A, B, C) & Observation Horizon

Steady background load mixes bulk science transfers (BULK_, 400–700 KB every 14–20 s across 0..119), routine telemetry (TELEM_NORM_, 32–64 KB every 30–45 s to Managers 120..125), and critical fault dispatches (CRITICAL_FAULT_, 16–32 KB every 90–140 s to Managers). Superimposed onto this baseline in CompB Stress/Benign are three multi-timescale traffic disturbances, each paired with Manager downlink throttle and release waves:

  • Event A (3,600–3,900 s, 5 min acute burst): BULK_BURST5M_ arrives every 1–2 s (500–900 KB). Wave W1 issues throttle commands at 3,600 s and nominal release at 3,900 s. Stale throttling is measured after 3,900 s.
  • Event B (7,200–9,000 s, 30 min shock): BULK_SHOCK30M_ arrives every 2–3 s (500–900 KB), paired with W2 (7,200 s / 9,000 s).
  • Event C (21,600–28,800 s, 2 h sustained regime shift): BULK_SHIFT2H_ arrives every 5–8 s (500–800 KB), paired with W3 (21,600 s / 28,800 s).

Crucially, DtnmaRlMetricsReport evaluates each event purely over the cohort of bundles created inside [t_start, t_end) and measures delivery within a fixed 3,600 s (1 h) post-creation horizon. Because the latest disturbance (Event C) closes at 28,800 s (8.0 h) plus a 3,600 s horizon (9.0 h)—well ahead of endTime = 43,200 s (12.0 h)—zero bundles suffer right-censoring, and short bursts are never diluted by hours of calm traffic.

4.3 Architectural Equivalence (E1, E2) & LOC Reuse Parity (A3)

  • E1 Strict Parity: When equivalenceConnOuterOrder = true, Tier 1 ManagedSprayAndWaitRouter reproduces hard-coded PrioritySprayAndWaitRouter bit-for-bit on MessageStatsReport across 11/11 seeds (0.0000 pp delta, 0 critical loss). On DtnmaRlMetricsReport, 10/11 seeds match identically across non-control metrics; seed 7103 differs by 0.0001 in avg_energy_soc (0.4055 vs 0.4054) solely due to periodic 16 B management beacon radio energy expenditure.
  • E2 Default Ordering TOST Equivalence: With standard global critical-first ordering (equivalenceConnOuterOrder = false), the mean paired bulk delta is -0.3100 pp (90% CI strictly within ±1.0 pp, p_TOST = 2.288e-6).
  • A3 Policy Reusability vs. Bespoke Code: A hand-coded subclass (EnergyAwareEpidemicRouter, 394 non-comment lines) reaches 70.36% bulk (98.66% crit, 125.4 alive) in Blackout—only +3.39 pp above uniform Tier 2 (+3.14 pp above Tier 3). Consequently, a single 12-line declarative rule file (rules_vdtn.txt) atop shared ADTNM adapters (253.5 mean LOC) recovers ~97% of specialized Java router performance portably across four protocols.

6. Honest Negatives Within Frozen Confirmatory Data

WARNING

ESSENTIAL METHODOLOGICAL DISCLOSURES 1. Failed Original Survival Non-Inferiority (H2_orig): The initially formulated survival non-inferiority test (M2 within -5.0 pp of M1-U at end of 12 h stress) failed: M2 yielded -5.48 ± 1.96 pp fewer surviving nodes than M1-U (83.8 vs 90.7/126, 0/11 wins, p_unadj = 9.646e-5). The primary confirmatory H2 hypothesis was updated to Event C bulk delivery in the study ledger, and the failed survival non-inferiority check is reported here transparently. 2. Optional M3 RL Module Underperforms Deterministic SRL (M2): Across every stress and benign endpoint, ShieldedCmdpRlAgent (20-feature linear Q-learning) preserved safety (0 critical lost via DtnmaSafetyShield) yet trailed M2 on bulk (63% vs 66% stress; 80% vs 82% benign), survival (76.0 vs 83.8), and stale throttle (5.5 vs 0.0). 3. Pareto Non-Dominance: No single configuration simultaneously wins every metric. Pre-installed static protection (M0c) maximizes stress survival (126/126) at severe benign cost (54% bulk), whereas remote control (M1-U) retains higher end-of-mission survivors (90.7) at the cost of persistent Event A stale throttling (389.1) and poor Event C delivery (47.8%).

Key Analytical Insights from Exploratory Controls

  1. Attribution of M2's Survival: Static SoC threshold M0e-25 matches M2 identically on 12 h survival (83.8 vs 83.8/126, p = 1.0), whereas M2-LocalOnly without remote updates finishes at 80.0/126 (+6.4 nodes over M0e-20, -3.8 behind M2). This isolates two orthogonal effects: local SRL rules deliver agile congestion relief (+8.16 pp Event C bulk over M0e-25 and 81.4–82.0% benign bulk), while adopting the elevated 0.25 battery threshold supplied the late-mission survival lift.
  2. Fair Best-Case Remote Flooding (M1-F-Group): Replacing legacy per-target unicast floods (M1-F: 118.7 kJ) with one shared group bundle per wave slashes control energy by 589× down to 201.6 J and achieves higher whole-mission survival (99.5/126) and stress bulk (74.57%) than M2. Nevertheless, because wave W1 propagation exhibits a 482.9 s median adoption latency (841.1 s across 90% of nodes)—even when triggered deterministically at t = 3,601 s—it still arrives after the 300 s Event A burst closes (117.5 stale node-s/N vs 0.0 in M2), lags M2 during Event C (46.66% vs 68.61%), and reduces benign bulk (76.01% vs 82.04%).

7. Threats to Validity & Reproducibility Verification

  • Oracle Downlink Wave Timing: Remote Manager scenarios (M1-U, M1-F-Group) inject policy waves at fixed scenario timestamps matching disturbance boundaries; a deployed central controller would experience additional uplink detection lag prior to dispatch.
  • Unvalidated Auxiliary Policies: scenarios/rules_uav.txt and continuous EDD_ENERGY_DRAIN telemetry exist in code as exploratory artifacts outside the v1.0 experimental matrix.
  • Post-Freeze Regression Parity: Re-running M0b, M1-U, and M2 on {7103, 7109} verified 6/6 SHA-256 identity on MessageStatsReport and DtnmaRecoveryTimelineReport plus exact non-CPU matching on DtnmaRlMetricsReport against the frozen v1.0-freeze baseline.

Chapter 7: Scenario Anatomy & Hands-On Tutorials

Estimated Completion Time: 10–15 minutes across all walkthroughs.
Verified Environment: Java JDK 17+ (tested on 24), Python 3.10+, and The ONE (../the-one). On Windows PowerShell, set $env:PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE = '1' to keep __pycache__ out of source trees.

Tutorial 0: Anatomy of an ADTNM Scenario File (.txt)

Every experiment in scenarios/*.txt configures five declarative blocks read sequentially by The ONE's Settings parser. Understanding these blocks makes any simulation campaign immediately transparent:

# 1. Clock & Simulation Horizon
Scenario.name = CompB_MultiScale_%%Group.router%%_%%MovementModel.rngSeed%%
Scenario.updateInterval = 0.5          # Discrete simulator tick (seconds)
Scenario.endTime = 43200               # 12 hours total (prevents event right-censoring)

# 2. Coprime Parameter Sweeps (Cartesian Product)
Group.router = [SprayAndWaitRouter; DtnmaM0bStaticRouter; ...; DtnmaM3RlRouter]  # 8 modes
MovementModel.rngSeed = [7103; 7109; ...; 7207]                                  # 11 primes -> 88 runs
Group.bufferSize = 10M                 # Field RAM capacity (5M Overload, 15M Blackout, 10M CompB)
Group.msgTtl = 300                     # Bundle expiration (minutes)

# 3. Heterogeneous Radio, Mobility & Battery Energy Budgets
btInterface.transmitSpeed = 250k       # Field Bluetooth-class radio (35 m range)
highspeedInterface.transmitSpeed = 10M # Backbone tram/relay radio (1,000 m range)
Group.initialEnergy = 2650, 3650       # Stress random draw [2650, 3650] J; idle scan = 0.05 W, TX = 0.90 W

# 4. ADTNM Management Engine Bindings
DtnmaRouter.configFile = scenarios/dtnma_params_default.txt
DtnmaRouter.rulesFile = scenarios/rules_vdtn.txt   # Local declarative SRL policy
Group.rulesFile = scenarios/rules_vdtn.txt

# 5. Multi-Class Traffic, Disruption Cohorts & Synchronized Reporting
Events1.prefix = BULK_                 # Background bulk transfers (400-700 KB every 14-20 s)
Events3.prefix = CRITICAL_FAULT_       # Priority emergency dispatches to Managers (16-32 KB)
Events4.time = 3600, 3900              # Event A acute 5-minute burst (paired with Manager wave W1)
Report.report1 = DtnmaRlMetricsReport  # Per-class, Event A/B/C cohort, & # WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF metrics
Report.report3 = DtnmaAuditReport      # Per-decision 16-column ARI provenance trace

Notice two subtle best practices used across the repository: - Coprime Array Counts: tools/parallel_batch_runner.py verifies that swept parameter arrays (e.g., 8 routers × 11 seeds) resolve cleanly without accidental index aliasing (--dry-run previews every run name). - Zero Right-Censoring: Setting Scenario.endTime = 43200 gives Event C (21,600–28,800 s) a full 3,600 s evaluation horizon plus 10,800 s spare margin.

Tutorial 1: Sync, Compile & Run DtnmaUnitTests (< 2 min)

The recommended one-step installer (install.py) links ADTNM sources and scenarios into a sibling the-one checkout, or you can compile manually against the-one/target:

$env:PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE = '1'
$THE_ONE = "n:\R&D\cog\the-one"
$ADTNM   = "n:\R&D\cog\ADTNM"

# Option A: Standard install & compile via installer
# python "$ADTNM\install.py" --one-dir "$THE_ONE"

# Option B: Direct javac compile + run 27 unit tests (30 check() assertions)
javac -cp "$THE_ONE\target;$THE_ONE\lib\*" -d "$THE_ONE\target" `
  "$ADTNM\src\routing\*.java" "$ADTNM\src\report\*.java" "$ADTNM\tests\DtnmaUnitTests.java"
java -cp "$THE_ONE\target;$THE_ONE\lib\*" DtnmaUnitTests

Expected Output Tail: Results: 27 passed, 0 failed. (spanning Test1a..Test22 across 30 check() assertions).

Tutorial 2: Run 1-Hour Smoke Scenario & Inspect All 3 Reports (~15 s)

To keep the repository free of stray output files during exploration, redirect Report.reportDir to a temporary scratch folder via a lightweight overlay file:

$SCRATCH = "$env:TEMP\adtnm_smoke"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$SCRATCH\reports" | Out-Null
((Get-Content "$ADTNM\scenarios\scenario_dtnma.txt") + "`nReport.reportDir = $($SCRATCH.Replace('\','/'))/reports/") | Set-Content "$SCRATCH\smoke.txt"

Push-Location $THE_ONE
java -Xmx512m -cp "$THE_ONE\target;$THE_ONE\lib\*" core.DTNSim -b 1 "$SCRATCH\smoke.txt"
Pop-Location

Get-Content "$SCRATCH\reports\Dtnma_Benchmark_MessageStatsReport.txt" -TotalCount 10
Get-Content "$SCRATCH\reports\Dtnma_Benchmark_DtnmaAuditReport.txt" | Select-String "AUDIT_SUMMARY"

Expected Observations: MessageStatsReport reports created: 262, delivered: 184 (delivery_prob: 0.7023, overhead_ratio: 6.7663). DtnmaAuditReport logs 2,400 decisions with traceable_ari_ratio: 1.0000 (33,468.50 B/node-hr). (Note: DtnmaDecisionReport counts harmless Tier 1 ACK-pruned duplicate evictions (53) inside its generic drop total; inspect unique_critical_lost in DtnmaRlMetricsReport to confirm 0 live critical message loss.)

Tutorial 3: Author Custom SRL Rules & Verify 100% Replay (< 3 min)

Create $SCRATCH\my_custom_rules.txt enforcing battery protection below SoC < 0.30 and surge throttling above Q >= 0.80 with an explicit PRIORITY: 10 catch-all nominal recovery rule:

RULE: ARI://DTNMA/SRL/CUSTOM_BATT_GUARD | PRIORITY: 100 | DESC: Custom battery survival guard
IF: (EDD_ENERGY_SOC < 0.30) || (EDD_CRIT_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.50)
THEN: CTRL_SET_SPRAY_QUOTA(1); CTRL_SET_INGRESS_MODE(2); CTRL_SET_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL(600); CTRL_SET_BACKPRESSURE(true)

RULE: ARI://DTNMA/SRL/CUSTOM_SURGE | PRIORITY: 80 | DESC: Custom queue surge throttle
IF: (EDD_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.80) && (EDD_QUEUE_DRIFT >= 0.005)
THEN: CTRL_SET_SPRAY_QUOTA(2); CTRL_SET_INGRESS_MODE(1); CTRL_SET_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL(300); CTRL_SET_BACKPRESSURE(true)

RULE: ARI://DTNMA/SRL/CUSTOM_NOMINAL | PRIORITY: 10 | DESC: Nominal catch-all recovery
IF: (EDD_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.0)
THEN: CTRL_SET_SPRAY_QUOTA(6); CTRL_SET_INGRESS_MODE(0); CTRL_SET_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL(60); CTRL_SET_BACKPRESSURE(true)

Append DtnmaRouter.intelligenceMode = STATIC_RULES, DtnmaRouter.rulesFile, and Group.rulesFile (using /-separated paths) in your scratch overlay scenario and run core.DTNSim -b 1. Inspect DtnmaAuditReport.txt to observe ARI://DTNMA/SRL/CUSTOM_* provenance and run verify_audit_replay (tools/evaluate_autonomic_framework.py) to confirm 100.00% deterministic replay.

Tutorial 4: Manage Any Stock ONE Router via DtnmaManagedRouter (Adapter Pattern)

  1. Subclass your chosen ONE protocol (e.g., extends FirstContactRouter implements DtnmaManagedRouter).
  2. Add private final DtnmaAgent agent; initialized cleanly inside both constructors (new DtnmaAgent(this, s) and copy constructor new DtnmaAgent(this, r.agent)).
  3. Delegate update() (agent.onBeforeUpdate(SimClock.getTime()); super.update();), changedConnection(), createNewMessage(), checkReceiving(), and makeRoomForMessage().
  4. Keep native forwarding heuristics intact while sorting CRIT_/CTRL_ tuples first and gating non-direct BULK_ relays via agent.allowNonDirectBulkForward.
  5. Validate with DtnmaUnitTests and test Tier 1 (TIER1_PROTECTION_ONLY) against an unmanaged baseline.

Tutorial 5: Batch Dry-Run & Re-Running v1.0 Statistical Analyzers (< 1 min)

$env:PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE = '1'

Chapter 8: Design Evolution, Engineering Post-Mortems & Architectural Decisions

Scope: Traces ADTNM's empirical development from early single-router RL experiments through the architecture-first refactoring (v1.0-freeze and exploratory follow-ups), distilling seven engineering post-mortems and core Architectural Decision Records (ADRs).

1. Major Design Phases

Phase Core Transition Scientific Lesson Learned
Phase 1: Single-Router CMDP RL Initial shielded Expected SARSA prototype with continuous beacons and parameterized configuration (DtnmaConfig) Dynamic Lagrangian lambda multipliers oscillated during multi-timescale traffic bursts; safety had to be hard-enforced deterministically rather than learned asymptotically.
Phase 2: Composable Substrate Pivot Extracted DtnmaAgent and DtnmaManagedRouter interface (Managed*Router adapters) separating management from routing Reduced per-protocol integration cost from ~400 lines of subclass logic to ~253.5 lines of thin delegation hooks while enabling portable .txt policy files.
Pilot Diagnostics & Pre-Freeze Protocol Introduced atomic decision-time snapshots, separated CritQ shield gates, added Tier 1–3 ablation, and split ACK-pruned evictions Eliminated 41% idle over-throttling and 0.1% tick-timing replay drift; demonstrated 100.00% deterministic offline audit replay.
Confirmatory v1.0 & Post-Freeze Controls Executed 627 held-out confirmatory urban VDTN runs (7103–7207), followed by 176 exploratory control runs (7211–7307) on M0e-20/25, M2-LocalOnly, and M1-F-Group Exposed the trade-off between stress survival and benign throughput, isolated the 0.25 energy-guard contribution, and confirmed M3 RL trails M2 SRL.

2. Seven Empirical Engineering Post-Mortems

PM-1: Unintended Over-Throttling of Idle Agents (41% -> 1.8% P0 Occupancy)

Early pilot runs locked healthy nodes into SAFE_EMERGENCY_HOLD (P0) for 41% of decision epochs, severely depressing normal bulk throughput. Investigation revealed two interacting flaws: the shield's S1 rule inspected only aggregate queue fill Q without distinguishing critical message saturation (CritQ), and early RL hold penalties distorted action preferences. Separating CritQ >= 0.35 / 0.50 thresholds from BULK_ occupancy in DtnmaSafetyShield and rebalancing epoch rewards dropped idle P0 hold time to 1.8% cleanly.

PM-2: Resolving a 0.1% Replay Drift via Atomic Pre-Decision Snapshots

Offline verification initially flagged minor rule-evaluation discrepancies (~0.1% of epochs) where a queue hovered right across a rule threshold. Logging was sampling host buffer occupancy after transfers within the tick rather than capturing the exact vector seen by the rule engine. Locking an immutable pre-decision snapshot (eddSnapshot[11]) atomically ahead of evaluation brought offline replay fidelity to 100.00% across 27.1 million audited rows.

PM-3: Why Whole-Mission Averages Mask Short Surges (Event A Cohort Tracking)

Over 12-hour runs, short 5-minute acute bursts (Event A, 3600–3900 s) were numerically washed out by long periods of moderate load. Introducing fixed-horizon creation-cohort windows (Events A, B, C with a 3,600 s observation horizon before endTime = 43,200 s) prevented right-censoring and quantified remote stale throttling (389.1 node-s/N in M1-U vs 0.0 in M2).

PM-4: Avoiding Broadcast Strawmen with Single-Copy Group Flooding (M1-F-Group)

The initial flooded remote baseline (M1-F) transmitted 120 individual per-destination bundles across the network (118.7 kJ), burning out batteries cleanly (13.5/126 alive). Post-freeze exploratory evaluation added M1-F-Group (one shared group-addressed wave bundle), slashing flooding energy by 589× to 201.6 J and rescuing 99.5/126 stress survivors—demonstrating fairly that even near-optimal remote flooding (482.9 s median adoption) remains slower than local sub-minute autonomy (300 s surges).

PM-5: Honest Reporting of Failed Survival Non-Inferiority (H2_orig)

Pre-registered survival non-inferiority (M2 within -5.0 pp of M1-U at 12 h stress) failed at -5.48 ± 1.96 pp (83.8 vs 90.7/126, 0/11 wins). Rather than hiding the shortfall after shifting H2 to Event C bulk, both outcomes are reported side-by-side in Chapter 6 alongside exploratory M0e-25 and M2-LocalOnly causal decomposition.

PM-6: Why Primal-Dual Lagrangian (lambda) Was Retired

Dynamic dual lambda updates could not track non-stationary multi-timescale DTN congestion fast enough, causing overshoot during sudden bursts. Hard constraints were consolidated into deterministic bitmask gating (DtnmaSafetyShield), leaving zeroed lambda = 0.0 fields purely as backward-compatible configuration shims.

PM-7: Separating ACK-Pruned Duplicates from Live Critical Loss

In the 1 h smoke scenario, DtnmaDecisionReport reports 53 critical drops whereas DtnmaRlMetricsReport records unique_critical_lost: 0 (critical_buffer_dropped_acked: 53). The 53 evictions were redundant replicas already acknowledged via 4 B contact ACKs (Tier 1 reclamation) rather than live message losses. Filtering ACKed duplicates cleanly inside DtnmaDecisionReport remains queued for a future code release.

3. Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)

ADR Architectural Decision Rejected Alternative Primary Rationale
ADR-01 Substrate Composition (DtnmaManagedRouter) Rewriting routing subclasses (EnergyAwareEpidemic) Cuts per-protocol code to ~253.5 LOC adapters + portable 12-line rule files
ADR-02 Finite 8-Profile Action Catalog (P0..P7) Continuous tuning of L and bpRatio Guarantees O(8) bitmask safety decidability (11111100) & clean ARI logs
ADR-03 Three-Tier Experimental Ablation (T1/T2/T3) Single monolithic enable toggle Isolates critical protection (T1) & ingress/energy policy (T2) from routing changes (T3)
ADR-04 Transparent Disclosure of Weak RL (M3) Parameter tuning to fit a single scenario Maintains integrity: deterministic SRL beats online linear Q-learning in v1.0
ADR-05 Strict Seed & Freeze Separation Mixing post-freeze tuning with 7103..7207 seeds Keeps 627 frozen confirmatory VDTN runs byte-reproducible (6/6 regression verified)

Because Event A's traffic spike runs only from 3600–3900 s (300 s duration), 75% of M1-F-Group nodes (and ~90% of M1-U nodes) adopt the throttle command after 3900 s — turning even best-case remote flooding into stale post-event throttling (117.5 stale node-s/N mean vs 0.0 for M2).

Example 6: Explaining Smoke Test 53 Critical Drops vs. 0 unique_critical_lost

From 1-Hour Smoke Run (scenario_dtnma.txt): - MessageStatsReport: created = 262, delivered = 184, delivery_prob = 0.7023, overhead_ratio = 6.7663 - DtnmaDecisionReport: Critical Fault Messages Dropped: 53 - DtnmaRlMetricsReport: unique_critical_lost = 0, critical_buffer_dropped = 0, critical_buffer_dropped_acked = 53

Reconciliation: Once CRIT_ bundles reach their destination, peers exchange 4 B ACK IDs and move redundant replicas from protected Tier 4 down into Tier 1 (deliveredAckSet). When bulk traffic later needs RAM, Tier 1 safely evicts those 53 already-delivered duplicate copies, freeing buffer space with 0 live information loss — whereas DtnmaDecisionReport.messageDeleted aggregates Tier 1 ACK-pruned copies together with un-ACKed drops.

Appendix A: Alignment with IETF RFC 9675 & IRTF RFC 7575

Scope Statement: ADTNM is RFC 9675-inspired and RFC 7575-inspired for architectural separation inside The ONE simulator. It does not implement wire-format CBOR encodings, formally authored YANG/ADM schemas, or ION runtime interoperability, and makes zero claim of certification or affiliation with external organizations.

1. Concept Mapping vs. IETF RFC 9675 (DTN Management Architecture, Nov 2024)

RFC 9675 Section / Concept RFC Requirement / Architectural Goal ADTNM Implementation (d4a159f) Explicit Difference / Boundary
Sec 3.1–3.2: Agent & Manager Roles Managers issue declarative guidance asynchronously; Agents monitor locally & act without polling DtnmaAgent runs closed-loop autonomously per node; remote scenario hosts emit delayed CTRL_ overlays (M1-U, M1-F-Group, M2) Remote Manager schedules in v1.0 scenarios are pre-scripted waves (Ch. 6 / Open Decision 3), not an interactive Manager daemon
Sec 4.1: Application Resource Identifiers (ARIs) Unambiguous compact naming for managed objects, rules, telemetry, and controls String URIs (ARI://DTNMA/SRL/<ID>, ARI://DTNMA/SHIELD/<GUARD>, ARI://DTNMA/RL/DIRECT) logged on 100% of decisions Text URIs serialized in Java/TSV audit files rather than CBOR-encoded binary DTNMA ARIs
Sec 4.2: Externally Defined Data (EDDs) Standardized node-sampled operational metrics decoupled from internal protocol structures 11 immutable EDD_* metrics in EddTelemetrySampler.java:26-36 sampled uniformly across all routers Java double[11] array indexed by enum; custom ADMs are not loaded dynamically
Sec 4.3: Controls (Actuators) Parameterized node actions altering behavior without code reloads 4 ControlAction primitives + 8 discrete profiles (P0..P7) driving L, bp, ing hooks via DtnmaManagedRouter Discrete finite gear box (P0..P7) chosen for O(8) shield decidability
Sec 4.4: State-Based Autonomy (SRL) Onboard event-condition-action rules evaluated continuously while disconnected DtnmaRuleParser loads RULE / IF / THEN files (rules_vdtn.txt) evaluated every 1.0 s (M2) Flat conjunction (&&) or disjunction (||) clauses; rules do not call custom external scripts

2. Concept Mapping vs. IRTF RFC 7575 (Autonomic Networking, June 2015)

RFC 7575 Principle Autonomic Goal ADTNM Mechanism (04a–04d) Boundary / Empirical Status
Sec 3.1: Self-Configuring Automatically adopt configuration changes upon context shift or intent update upsertDownlinkOverlayRule() integrates remote CTRL_ waves seamlessly (PRIO 100) without restart Remote waves limited to profile/guard clamps in v1.0
Sec 3.1: Self-Healing Recover normal capacity automatically once transient disturbance passes Catch-all recovery rules (PRIORITY: 10, e.g., VDTN_URBAN_NOMINAL) + 126/126 recovery across overload (CompA) Missing catch-all recovery rule in unvalidated experimental rules_uav.txt
Sec 3.1: Self-Optimizing Improve throughput/latency continuously within safe resource budgets Optional M3 (ShieldedCmdpRlAgent) explores Q-values (P0..P7); local backpressure (bp) spares hot peers M3 is Implemented, experimental and trailed M2 in v1.0
Sec 3.1: Self-Protecting Defend critical availability & energy survival against storms or battery depletion DtnmaSafetyShield (S1–S4) + 5-tier buffer reserve + Tier 1 ACK pruning (0 critical loss across 132 CompA runs) Relies on honest bundle prefixes (CRIT_, CTRL_); no cryptographic auth
Sec 4: Explicit Non-Goals Autonomy operates strictly inside designer bounds; deterministic auditability preserved Hard S1–S4 bitmask blocks unsafe actions + atomic 100.00% DtnmaAuditReport offline replay Hard shield overrides (OVERRIDE column) remain traceable to specific EDD readings

3. Related IETF/IRTF Protocols Referenced Accurately

  • RFC 9171 (Bundle Protocol Version 7, S. Burleigh, K. Fall, E. Birrane, III, IETF Proposed Standard, January 2022) — Store-carry-forward bundle model emulated in The ONE.
  • RFC 6693 (Probabilistic Routing Protocol for Intermittently Connected Networks [PRoPHET], A. Lindgren, A. Doria, E. Davies, S. Grasic, IRTF Experimental, August 2012) — Managed substrate implemented by ProphetV2Router / ManagedProphetV2Router.

Appendix B: Alphabetical Glossary & Acronym Index

Every acronym and domain term used across the ADTNM Study Guide and root README.md is defined concisely here.

  • ACK (Delivery Acknowledgment): 4 B bundle ID notification exchanged on contact (<= 32 IDs / contact, LRU 512) so peers move delivered CRIT_ replicas into Tier 1 for safe reclamation.
  • ADTNM (Autonomic DTN Management): Architectural management layer implemented atop The ONE decoupling policy (DtnmaAgent) from routing substrates (Managed*Router).
  • AoI (Age of Information): Time elapsed (AoI(t) = t - t_last_rx) since the last remote Manager uplink/downlink status update arrived, sampled every 10 s.
  • ARI (Application Resource Identifier): RFC 9675-inspired URI tag (e.g., ARI://DTNMA/SRL/VDTN_SURGE_THROTTLE, ARI://DTNMA/SHIELD/DENSE_STORM_GUARD) emitted per decision in DtnmaAuditReport.
  • AST / Predicate Expression: Structured comparison clause list (>, <, >=, <=, ==, != combined via && or ||) compiled by DtnmaRuleParser.
  • Backpressure Guard (bp): Hop-by-hop check (allowNonDirectBulkForward) blocking non-direct BULK_ forwarding whenever Q_nbr > Q_local - bpRatio.
  • BULK_ (SCIENCE_DATA_): Low-priority delay-tolerant bundle class (Tier 0 eviction target).
  • CMDP (Constrained Markov Decision Process): Mathematical framing motivating M3 (ShieldedCmdpRlAgent); dynamic primal-dual lambda updates were retired (lambda = 0.0), leaving hard safety guarantees strictly to DtnmaSafetyShield.
  • CRIT_ (CRITICAL_FAULT_): High-priority mission-critical fault telemetry (Tier 4 protection while un-ACKed).
  • CTRL_ (CTRL_UPDATE_, CTRL_GROUP_): Remote Manager control bundles carrying priority-100 temporary overlay configurations.
  • DTN (Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Network): Sparse intermittent network relying on store-carry-forward routing (RFC 9171).
  • DTNMA (DTN Management Architecture): Architecture specified in IETF RFC 9675 (Nov 2024).
  • EDD (Externally Defined Data): Standardized 11-element telemetry vector sampled by EddTelemetrySampler.
  • E1 / E2 Equivalence: E1 = exact bit-for-bit Tier 1 parity (ManagedSprayAndWait vs PrioritySprayAndWait); E2 = statistical equivalence via Two One-Sided Tests (TOST, +/- 1.0 pp).
  • EWMA (Exponentially Weighted Moving Average): Smoothing filter used for EDD_QUEUE_DRIFT (α = 0.30) and EDD_NODE_SPEED (α = 0.25).
  • Holm-Bonferroni: Sequential multiple-comparison correction (m = 4) protecting the confirmatory CompB hypothesis family (H1–H4).
  • Managed Substrate: Stock forwarding algorithm (Epidemic, PRoPHETv2, MaxProp, SprayAndWait, DtnmaRouter) governed through DtnmaManagedRouter.
  • ONE (The Opportunistic Network Environment): Discrete-event Java DTN simulator (0.1 s–0.5 s tick step) hosting ADTNM.
  • P0..P7 (DtnmaPolicyProfile): Eight immutable actuator configurations varying replica quota L (1..12), bpRatio (0.05..0.30), and ingressMode (0..2).
  • R1 Deterministic Replay: Offline verification confirming 100.00% of audited rows reproduce identical ARIs, actions, and 8-bit safety masks.
  • RL (Reinforcement Learning): Experimental 20-feature linear Q-critic (M3, ShieldedCmdpRlAgent, Implemented, experimental).
  • SoC (State of Charge): Normalized remaining battery ratio Erem / Einit ∈ [0, 1] (EDD_ENERGY_SOC).
  • SRL (State-Based Rule): Declarative local autonomy rule (RULE / IF / THEN) parsed from .txt scenario rule sets.
  • T50 / T90: Median / 90th-percentile time (s) from Manager wave emission until 50% / 90% of target agents adopt the downlink bundle (# WAVE_ADOPTION_CDF).
  • vDTN (Vehicular DTN): Urban vehicular delay-tolerant traffic & ITS regime (rules_vdtn.txt, compA_vdtn_overload).

Week 1 Guided Onboarding Plan (onboarding_week1_plan.md)

Objective: Equip any newcomer without prior DTN, RFC, or simulator experience to build and run ADTNM, write custom autonomic rules, and critically interpret empirical evaluations within five focused half-day sessions.

Session Learning Focus Core Readings (docs/study-guide/) Practical Lab Exercise
Day 1 DTN fundamentals & managed-substrate framing 01 Executive Summary, 02 Primer, 03 Architecture Compile via Tutorial 1, pass all 27/27 unit tests, and summarize why routers act as managed substrates
Day 2 Scenario files, logs & drop accounting 04a Mechanisms, 07 Scenario Guide & Tutorials, Worked Example 6 Run Tutorial 2 (1 h smoke: 262 created / 184 delivered) and reconcile ACK-pruned copies vs live losses
Day 3 State-based rules, safety shield & audit replay 04b Mechanisms, Worked Examples 1–3, Tutorial 3 Author a custom RULE/IF/THEN policy with a PRIORITY: 10 catch-all rule and verify 100.00% ARI replay
Day 4 Adapter architecture & codebase navigation 04c Mechanisms, 05 Codebase Tour, Worked Examples 4–5 Compare ManagedEpidemicRouter.java against EnergyAwareEpidemicRouter.java and preview parallel_batch_runner.py --dry-run
Day 5 Empirical rigor & honest negative results 06 Evaluation & Results, 08 History & Decisions, Appendix A Contrast confirmatory H1–H4 against exploratory controls (M0e-25, M1-F-Group), failed H2_orig, and M3 RL limitations

2. Core Data Flow & Hard Shield (S1–S4)

11 EDDs (EddTelemetrySampler) -> SRL Rules / [Opt. M3 RL] -> DtnmaSafetyShield (mask[0]=true) -> P0..P7 -> DtnmaManagedRouter -> DtnmaAuditReport (ARI://...) - S1 Critical Buffer: CritQ >= 0.50 || (Q >= 0.94 && dQ >= 0.015) -> {P0} | CritQ >= 0.35 || (Q >= 0.82 && dQ > 0.015) -> {P0, P1, P2} - S2 Battery: SoC < shieldEnergyMin (0.20 / 0.25) -> {P0, P1} | S3 Dense Storm: Q >= 0.78 && Dens >= 5.0 -> block {P6, P7} | S4 Remote Clamp

3. Control Profiles (DtnmaPolicyProfile) & Queue Eviction Order (O(N))

P0 SAFE_EMERGENCY_HOLD (L=1, ing=2, bp=.05) | P1 SAFE_THROTTLE_STRICT (L=2, ing=1, bp=.08) | P2..P3 BALANCED (L=4..6, ing=0, bp=.10..12) | P4 STANDARD (L=6, bpOff) | P5..P7 SPRAY (L=8..12) - Evict First -> Last: Tier 0 BULK_ -> Tier 1 ACKed CRIT_ -> Tier 2 Stale -> Tier 3 Active CTRL_ -> Tier 4 Live CRIT_

4. Rule Syntax (rules_vdtn.txt) & Key Config Keys

RULE: ARI://DTNMA/SRL/ID | PRIORITY: 80 | DESC: ...
IF: (EDD_QUEUE_RATIO >= 0.88) && (EDD_QUEUE_DRIFT >= 0.008)
THEN: CTRL_SET_SPRAY_QUOTA(2); CTRL_SET_INGRESS_MODE(1); CTRL_SET_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL(300); CTRL_SET_BACKPRESSURE(true)

Keys: Group.rulesFile, DtnmaRouter.configFile, interventionTier (TIER1..TIER3), intelligenceMode (STATIC_RULES vs SHIELDED_CMDP_RL), shieldEnergyMin.

5. Headline Numbers (provenance_ledger.json) & Cautions

  • Negatives & Exploratory (7211..7307, p_unadj): H2_orig survival NI failed (-5.48 pp, 0/11); M3 RL lost to M2; M0e-25 tied M2 stress survival (83.8 vs 83.8, M2-LocalOnly = 80.0); M1-F-Group (201.6 J, 99.5 alive, T50=483 s) misses Event A (300 s).

Supervisor & Reviewer Audit Checklist (supervisor_review_checklist.md)

Use this verification checklist when auditing the thesis manuscript, architecture documentation, or subsequent v1.1 experimental extensions.

  • [ ] Architecture-First Framing: ADTNM is presented consistently as a cross-router management architecture (Managed*Router substrates governed by DtnmaAgent), rather than a standalone router.
  • [ ] Bounded RFC Positioning: RFC 9675 (Nov 2024) and RFC 7575 (June 2015) are cited accurately as conceptual inspiration, with zero claims of binary wire-format CBOR/ADM conformance or external institutional affiliation (Appendix A).
  • [ ] Disjoint Seed & Campaign Governance: Confirmatory claims rest solely on frozen seeds 7103–7207 (627 urban VDTN runs, Holm–Bonferroni corrected), while exploratory controls (v1.0-exp-controls) use fresh seeds 7211–7307 (176 runs, unadjusted p_unadj).
  • [ ] Transparent Disclosure of Negative Results: Both the failed survival non-inferiority test (-5.48 ± 1.96 pp, 0/11 wins) and the optional M3 RL planner's shortfall behind declarative SRL (M2) appear clearly in Chapters 1, 6, and 8.
  • [ ] Fair Causal Attribution: Stress survival comparisons explicitly present M0e-25 (83.8), M2 (83.8), M2-LocalOnly (80.0), and M1-F-Group (99.5 at 201.6 J, 482.9 s median adoption) side-by-side.
  • [ ] Scenario & Provenance Completeness: Every quantitative metric traces to provenance_ledger.json and appendix_d_provenance.md, backed by explicit scenario parameters in Chapter 6.
